Who compiled 'The Guiding Symptoms of our Materia Medica'?
Constantine Hering's Guiding Symptoms runs to ten volumes. Kent wrote the Lectures on Homoeopathic Materia Medica, Boericke the Pocket Manual and Allen the Keynotes.
The main source of the symptoms recorded in homoeopathic Materia Medica is:
provings of drugs on healthy human beings
Materia Medica is built chiefly from provings on healthy people, supplemented by toxicology and clinical observation.
Which remedy is described as the chronic of Ignatia?
Natrum mur. is the chronic of Ignatia; both cover ailments from grief, with Natrum mur. for the deep, long-standing state.
Which remedy is inimical to Phosphorus and should not be given immediately before or after it?
Causticum and Phosphorus are inimical. Arsenicum album is complementary to Phosphorus.
Which remedy is regarded as the chronic of Pulsatilla?
Silicea is the chronic of Pulsatilla. The two share a yielding, mild temperament and similar discharges.
Aggravation from the slightest motion, with relief from pressure and from lying on the painful side, is characteristic of:
Bryonia is worse from any motion and better from pressure. Rhus tox has the opposite modality, better from continued motion.
A feeling that the heart will stop beating unless the patient keeps moving is a keynote of:
Gelsemium fears the heart will stop unless he moves. Digitalis has the reverse: the heart will stop if he moves.
Complaints of sudden, violent onset after exposure to dry, cold wind, with intense fear of death and restlessness, call for:
Aconite: sudden onset after dry cold wind, fear of death, anxiety and restlessness. Belladonna is sudden too, but marked by heat, redness and throbbing.
Intolerance of milk in infants, with the milk vomited in large curds soon after feeding, indicates:
Aethusa's keynote is inability to digest milk, vomited in curds, followed by exhaustion and sleep.
After an injury the patient says nothing is the matter with him, the bed feels too hard, and the whole body feels sore and bruised. The remedy is:
Arnica: sore, bruised feeling, the bed feels too hard, and the patient insists he is well.
In a typhoid state the patient feels his body is scattered about the bed and tries to gather the pieces together. The remedy is:
This delusion is the classic keynote of Baptisia, alongside dusky face, offensive discharges and stupor.
One cheek red and hot, the other pale and cold; the child is extremely irritable during dentition and wants to be carried. The remedy is:
Chamomilla: one cheek red, the other pale, intolerable irritability and pain, quieted only by being carried.
Constant nausea that is not relieved by vomiting, with a clean tongue, is characteristic of:
Ipecac: persistent nausea, vomiting gives no relief, and the tongue stays clean. Antimonium crudum has a thick white tongue.
For punctured wounds where the injured part is cold to the touch yet relieved by cold applications, the indicated remedy is:
The remedy is Ledum palustre, which is not among options A to D. Coldness of the part with relief from cold is its keynote.
Agonising colic that is relieved by bending double and by hard pressure, often brought on by anger, calls for:
Colocynth: colic better bending double and from hard pressure, often after anger. Dioscorea is better from bending backwards.
Profuse, painless, gushing diarrhoea that is worse in the early morning suggests:
Podophyllum: profuse, painless, gushing, offensive stools, worse early morning. Veratrum album has diarrhoea with collapse and cold sweat.
Stiffness and pain that are worse on first motion, better from continued motion and worse in cold, damp weather point to:
Rhus tox: the rusty-gate modality, worse on beginning to move, better by continued motion, worse from damp cold.
A left-sided neuralgic headache that rises and falls with the sun is characteristic of:
Spigelia covers left-sided neuralgia increasing and decreasing with the sun. Sanguinaria has the right-sided version.
Ailments from suppressed anger and indignation, along with clean incised wounds, call for:
Staphisagria: effects of suppressed anger, humiliation or indignation, and incised wounds, including surgical ones.
Burning pains relieved by heat, great anxiety and restlessness, aggravation after midnight, and thirst for small quantities at short intervals indicate:
These are the classic generals of Arsenicum album, together with prostration out of proportion to the illness.
Desire for cold drinks, which are vomited as soon as they become warm in the stomach, is a keynote of:
Phosphorus craves cold drinks and vomits them once they warm in the stomach.
Coarse rattling of mucus in the chest with very little expectoration is characteristic of:
Antimonium tart.: loud rattling, little expectoration, drowsiness and weakness, especially in children and the old.
Anticipatory anxiety with hurriedness, and a craving for sweets which disagree and cause diarrhoea, indicate:
Argentum nitricum: hurried, anxious before events, craves sweets, which bring on flatulence and diarrhoea.
Extreme chilliness, so that the patient wants the head covered even in summer, with offensive discharges and despair of recovery, calls for:
Psorinum is very chilly, wants warm clothing in summer, has filthy-smelling discharges and despairs of recovery. Sulphur is a hot patient.
In septic states, a pulse out of proportion to the temperature is the keynote of:
Pyrogenium, prepared from decomposed meat, covers septic fevers with a pulse that does not match the temperature.
Who wrote 'Keynotes and Characteristics with Comparisons of some of the Leading Remedies of the Materia Medica'?
Henry Clay Allen wrote the Keynotes. Nash wrote 'Leaders in Homoeopathic Therapeutics'.
Which remedy is regarded as the chronic of Aconite?
Sulphur is the chronic of Aconite: it continues the work of Aconite in deeper, slower states.
Want of grit, offensive foot sweat and a tendency to expel foreign bodies such as splinters indicate:
Silicea: lack of stamina and confidence, offensive sweat of the feet, and expulsion of foreign bodies from the tissues.
A mild, yielding, weepy patient who is thirstless, has changeable symptoms and is better in the open air needs:
Pulsatilla: gentle, tearful, seeks consolation, thirstless, wandering symptoms, worse in a warm room and better in open air.
Craving for salt, aggravation at about 10 a.m. and aggravation from consolation point to:
Natrum mur.: salt craving, 10 to 11 a.m. aggravation, and dislike of consolation, which makes the patient worse.
Intolerable urging to urinate, with burning, cutting pains before, during and after urination, calls for:
Cantharis: violent burning and cutting pain with constant urging, passing urine drop by drop.
Extreme sensitiveness to cold air and to touch, splinter-like pains and a tendency to suppuration indicate:
Hepar sulph.: oversensitive to cold and touch, splinter-like pains, and inflammation that tends to suppurate.
Warts and condylomata, the fixed idea that the body is brittle like glass, and ill effects of vaccination point to:
Thuja: the chief antisycotic, with warty growths, the glass delusion and complaints following vaccination.
Stinging, burning pains with oedematous swelling, thirstlessness and relief from cold applications indicate:
Apis: bee-sting pains, puffy swelling, no thirst, worse from heat and better from cold.
Painlessness and stupor with stertorous breathing, and constipation with no urging at all, are characteristic of:
Opium: insensibility, deep stupor with snoring breathing, and complete inactivity of the bowels.
Comparative Materia Medica is mainly concerned with:
studying related remedies side by side to tell them apart
Comparative study sets similar remedies against each other, by modalities and characteristics, so the right one can be chosen.
A fat, fair, flabby child whose head sweats profusely during sleep, with slow dentition and a craving for eggs, needs:
Calcarea carb.: leucophlegmatic constitution, head sweat in sleep, late teething and walking, desire for eggs.
In the centesimal scale, the ratio of drug to vehicle at each step is:
One part of the previous potency to 99 parts of vehicle, a dilution of 1 in 100 at each step.
The decimal scale of potentisation was introduced by:
Hering introduced the decimal (1 in 10) scale. Hahnemann used the centesimal and, later, the LM scale.
In the 6th edition of the Organon, the 50 millesimal (LM) method of preparation is described in:
§270 gives the LM method. §269 deals with potentisation in general and §128 with provings in the 30th potency.
The Korsakovian method of potentisation uses:
a single vial, emptied and refilled at each step
a new vial at each step
a continuous flow of water through the vial
Korsakoff's method uses one vial throughout; the Hahnemannian method uses a fresh vial for each potency.
Trituration is the method used to prepare potencies of:
insoluble substances such as metals and minerals
Insoluble substances are ground with sugar of milk until they can be dissolved and potentised further.
The usual vehicle for trituration is:
Sugar of milk (Saccharum lactis) is hard, neutral and suits grinding.
In homoeopathic pharmacy, the symbol Φ denotes:
Φ marks the mother tincture, the starting preparation of a plant drug.
Which of the following is a sarcode?
Sarcodes come from healthy tissues or secretions, such as Thyroidinum. Psorinum and Medorrhinum are nosodes; X-ray is an imponderable.
The Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia Laboratory of the Government of India is located at:
The Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia Laboratory, set up in 1975, is at Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.
Good manufacturing practice for homoeopathic medicines is laid down in which Schedule of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules?
Schedule M-I sets the GMP requirements for homoeopathic medicines.
In a prescription, the symbol Rx forms the:
The superscription is Rx (recipe, take). The inscription names the medicine, the subscription instructs the dispenser and the signatura instructs the patient.
The abbreviation 'h.s.' on a prescription means:
'h.s.' (hora somni) means at bedtime, which is not among options A to D.
Beyond about which centesimal potency is it unlikely that even one molecule of the original substance remains?
At 12C the dilution is 10 to the power -24, beyond Avogadro's number (about 6 x 10 to the power 23).
'Similia similibus curentur' is correctly translated as:
Likes are always cured by likes
Let likes be cured by likes
Hahnemann wrote 'curentur' (subjunctive: let them be cured), a rule for the physician to follow, not 'curantur' (are cured).
According to §6, the unprejudiced observer perceives in each individual disease only:
the changes in health of body and mind that can be perceived by the senses
the material cause of the disease
the name given to the disease in textbooks
§6: the observer, free from speculation, notices only deviations from the former healthy state, felt by the patient, remarked by those around him and observed by the physician.
In Kent's observations, a quick, short and strong aggravation followed by rapid improvement indicates:
a correct remedy and good vitality: the best prognosis
an incurable case with tissue destruction
a wrong remedy that must be antidoted
Kent's third observation: the aggravation is quick, short and strong and is followed by rapid improvement, so the remedy suited and the reaction is vigorous.
Hahnemann held psora responsible for what share of all chronic diseases?
In The Chronic Diseases Hahnemann attributes about seven-eighths of chronic diseases to psora, the rest to syphilis and sycosis.
Over-growth, warts, infiltration of tissues and aggravation in damp weather are characteristic of:
Sycosis is the miasm of excess and over-production: warts, condylomata, thickening and catarrhal discharges, worse in humid weather.
According to §150, a trivial ailment of recent origin (an indisposition) should be handled by:
a slight change in diet and regimen, usually without medicine
an antipsoric remedy in high potency
a nosode of the prevailing miasm
§150: a few trivial symptoms observed only a short time are not a fully developed disease; altering the diet and regimen will usually dispel the indisposition.
The sixth edition of the Organon was first published, in German, in:
Hahnemann finished the manuscript in 1842, a year before his death; Richard Haehl published it in 1921.
'The Genius of Homoeopathy: Lectures and Essays on Homoeopathic Philosophy' was written by:
Stuart Close (1860-1929) published The Genius of Homoeopathy in 1924.
The first remedy improved the patient; the improvement has stopped and the same symptoms have returned unchanged. The second prescription should usually be:
a repetition of the same remedy
a new remedy chosen from the latest symptoms only
Kent: when the original symptoms return unchanged after a good effect, the remedy is still indicated and is repeated.
Rheumatic pains that are worse before a thunderstorm are a keynote of:
Rhododendron: dread of storms, with pains that come on before a thunderstorm and ease once it breaks.
Injuries to the periosteum and tendons, and eyestrain from fine work, call for:
Ruta: bruised periosteum, strained tendons and flexors, and aching eyes after close work.
Jealousy, obscene talk, a desire to uncover and foolish laughter point to:
Hyoscyamus: jealous, immodest and obscene, with silly laughter and twitching.
Which remedy is inimical to Rhus toxicodendron?
Apis and Rhus tox are inimical and should not follow each other. Bryonia is complementary to Rhus tox.
Ill effects of loss of sleep and night watching, with vertigo and nausea from riding in a carriage, call for:
Cocculus: exhaustion from nursing the sick through the night, and travel sickness with vertigo.
Profound melancholy with thoughts of suicide, and bone pains that are worse at night, indicate:
Aurum met.: deep depression with a longing to die, and syphilitic bone pains worse at night.
Stitching pains, aggravation between 2 and 4 a.m. and swelling of the upper eyelids are characteristic of:
Kali carb.: stitching pains, the 2 to 4 a.m. aggravation, and baggy swelling of the upper lids.
Profuse, offensive sweat that brings no relief, aggravation at night, and a moist, flabby, indented tongue with intense thirst point to:
Mercurius: worse at night and from the heat of the bed, sweats without relief, and has the moist tongue with thirst.
Which of the following is an imponderable?
Imponderabilia are drugs prepared from energy, such as X-ray, magnetism and electricity.
Nosodes come from diseased material, such as Psorinum, Medorrhinum and Tuberculinum. Healthy tissues give sarcodes.
By Hahnemann's method, how long does the trituration of one centesimal potency take?
Each potency takes one hour: three periods of 20 minutes, each of 6 minutes' grinding and 4 minutes' scraping, done twice.
After which trituration did Hahnemann convert a potency into liquid form?
After the third centesimal trituration the substance is soluble and is carried on as a liquid potency.
How many succussions are given at each step of the LM (50 millesimal) potency?
The 6th edition prescribes 100 strong succussions for each LM step. The 5th edition used 2 for centesimal potencies.
The first volume of the Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia of India was published in:
HPI Volume I appeared in 1971; further volumes followed.
The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, which also governs homoeopathic medicines, was passed in:
The Act dates from 1940. The Drugs and Cosmetics Rules followed in 1945.
Which of the following is NOT a vehicle in homoeopathic pharmacy?
Vehicles are neutral carriers with no medicinal action. Sulphur is a medicinal substance.
Hahnemann's experiment of 1790, which led him to the law of similars, was made with:
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. While translating Cullen's Materia Medica in 1790 he took cinchona himself and developed symptoms like intermittent fever.
According to §9, in the healthy condition the material organism is governed by:
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §9: in health the spirit-like vital force (dynamis) rules with unbounded sway and keeps all parts in harmonious operation.
In Kent's evaluation of mental symptoms, which group ranks highest?
Symptoms of the will (loves, hates, emotions)
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Kent ranks mental symptoms in the order will, understanding, memory.
Which miasm has the itch eruption as its primary manifestation?
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Psora is the chronic miasm whose primary outward sign is the itch (scabies-like) eruption.
A patient who feels his body is enormously enlarged and time passes too slowly, with exaltation and uncontrollable laughter, needs:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Cannabis indica: errors of time and space, exaltation.
Homesickness with red cheeks, burning pains like pepper and chilliness in fat, flabby people suggests:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Capsicum: nostalgia with red face; burning like cayenne.
Right-sided headache beginning in the occiput, settling over the right eye, rising and falling with the sun, suggests:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Sanguinaria is right-sided; Spigelia is left-sided.
Sleeplessness from excessive joy or pleasant surprise, with an over-active mind full of ideas, calls for:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Coffea: over-excitement of the mind and senses.
The remedy Lachesis is prepared from:
the venom of the bushmaster snake
Topic 3, Pharmacy. Lachesis muta, the South American bushmaster.
On a prescription, the 'inscription' is the part that gives:
the name and quantity of the medicine
Topic 3, Pharmacy. Superscription (Rx), inscription, subscription (directions to the pharmacist) and signatura (directions to the patient).

According to the demographic cycle, India is in (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):

Cadaveric spasm differs from rigor mortis because it:
occurs instantly at death and preserves the last act, such as grip on a weapon

Organon of the Healing Art (Organon der Heilkunst)
Organon of Rational Medicine (Organon der rationellen Heilkunde)

a superficial, palliative remedy, or an incurable patient
a correct remedy in the right potency

The most common pattern in irritable bowel syndrome is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. As keyed by GPSC.
The most important mechanism in GERD is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
frequent transient lower oesophageal sphincter relaxations
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Transient LES relaxations allow reflux.
Absence (petit mal) seizures show on EEG:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Treated with ethosuximide or valproate.

Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Rubella triad: PDA, cataract, deafness.
Kwashiorkor differs from marasmus chiefly by the presence of (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Oedema is the hallmark of kwashiorkor.

Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Virchow's node.

4 mL × body weight (kg) × % burn in 24 hours, half in the first 8 hours

'Tache noire' is a post-mortem sign seen:
on the skin of the back
in the eyes when the eyelids remain open

Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Constantine Hering described this direction of cure.

a good sign that the disease is being cured
a sign the remedy was wrong
a reason to change the remedy at once

Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §80: psora is the oldest, most universal and most pernicious chronic miasmatic disease.

the first stage of inflammations and fevers, before exudation

Topic 2, Materia Medica. Magnesia carb: sourness of the whole body.
Bacillinum, a tubercular nosode, is especially used for:
patients with a tubercular history and recurrent chest infections or ringworm
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Burnett introduced Bacillinum.
Remedies such as X-ray, Magnetis polus and Sol are drawn from which source?
Topic 3, Pharmacy. Imponderabilia are 'weightless' energies: X-ray, magnetism, sunlight, electricity.
The abbreviation 'p.r.n.' on a prescription means:
C. M. Boger's approach to repertorisation gave special importance to:
Topic 4, Repertory. Boger used pathological generals and causation.
Secretin stimulates the pancreas to secrete juice rich in:

Cortisol is secreted by the adrenal cortex zone called:
Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Glomerulosa = aldosterone; reticularis = androgens.
a thrombus formed in flowing blood (ante-mortem)

Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Leishmania donovani; LD bodies in splenic aspirate.
In a patient with Graves' disease, the thyroid profile shows (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Suppressed TSH with raised T3 and T4.
The Koebner phenomenon (lesions appearing at sites of injury) is typical of:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Also seen in lichen planus and vitiligo.
Urticaria with burning, stinging wheals, worse from heat and better from cold applications, calls for:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Apis: oedematous, stinging wheals, thirstless, better from cold.
Oligomenorrhoea, hirsutism, acne and multiple small ovarian follicles on ultrasound suggest:
Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Rotterdam criteria: two of anovulation, hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovaries.
Lower abdominal pain, fever, purulent vaginal discharge and cervical motion tenderness suggest:
Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. PID is an ascending infection; it risks infertility and ectopic pregnancy.
For blunt injuries, bruises and a sore, bruised feeling after a fall, the first remedy is:
Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Arnica is the trauma remedy for blunt injury and shock.
Punctured wounds that feel cold to touch yet are better from cold applications call for:
Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Ledum: puncture wounds, insect bites; cold yet better by cold.
The main objective of Tele-MANAS is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. National Tele Mental Health Programme, launched in 2022.
The core principle of the Alma-Ata Declaration (1978) is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
Health for All through primary health care
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Primary health care as the key.

laboratory reports before speaking to the patient
freedom from prejudice, sound senses, attention in observing and fidelity in recording
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §83: the unprejudiced observer; case taking demands freedom from prejudice and sound senses.

the totality of symptoms, with its accompanying circumstances
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §18: the sum of all the symptoms and circumstances is the sole indication.

Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. A remedy that is acting is left alone. Kent: when in doubt, wait.

Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Offensive, fish-brine discharges are a sycotic keynote.

Topic 2, Materia Medica. Natrum carb: worse from summer heat and mental exertion.

Topic 2, Materia Medica. Ceanothus is the classic spleen remedy.
Which remedy is complementary to Pulsatilla?
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Silicea is the chronic of Pulsatilla; Kali sulph is also complementary.

the juice and moisture content of the plant (Classes I to IX)
Topic 3, Pharmacy. The new HPI method uses a uniform drug strength.
'Strong alcohol' in the Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia of India is ethanol of about:

analysis and evaluation of symptoms, totality, repertorisation, then final selection from the materia medica
materia medica first, then case taking
Topic 4, Repertory. The repertory narrows the field; the materia medica decides.
The normal PR interval on the ECG is:
Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. It mainly reflects conduction delay in the AV node.
The normal serum anion gap is about:
Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Raised in diabetic ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, renal failure and some poisonings.
Red blood cell casts in urine indicate:

Blunting of the costophrenic angle on a chest X-ray suggests:

Recurrent abdominal pain related to defecation, with altered stool frequency or form and no structural disease, is:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Rome IV criteria for IBS; a functional disorder.
Asterixis (flapping tremor) in a cirrhotic patient suggests:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Also seen in CO2 retention and uraemia.

Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Targets are individualised; 7% suits most adults.
The commonest benign tumour of the uterus, a frequent cause of heavy menstrual bleeding, is the:
Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Fibroids are smooth-muscle tumours; they cause menorrhagia and infertility.

Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Rotavirus vaccine is in India's UIP.
Fractures that are slow to unite, with pricking pain at the site, are helped by:
Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Symphytum ('knitbone') promotes union of fractures.

Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Staphysagria: clean-cut wounds and post-operative pain.

infant mortality, literacy and life expectancy at age one
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. As keyed in GPSC Medical Officer, 2024.

Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. It raises serum calcium.

Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. The pneumococcus.

all existing cases at a point in time
new cases occurring in a defined period

Myocardium (and then the eyelids and face)

understands the nature, risks and alternatives of the procedure and agrees voluntarily

purely local, to be treated by external applications
an expression of an internal disease of the whole organism

marked tissue changes, though the patient may recover slowly

Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. A sensitive indicator of community health.

at the height of the chill

a heading under which remedies producing that symptom are listed

tight junctions of capillary endothelium in the brain

gravitational pooling of blood in dependent parts

psychological means such as confidence, friendly advice and reasoning

medicinal substances in food and drink, such as strong coffee, spices and perfumes

a repetition of the first remedy

Tonsillitis that begins on the left side and moves to the right, worse after sleep and from hot drinks, with intolerance of anything around the neck, suggests:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Lachesis: left to right, worse after sleep. Lycopodium goes right to left.
Hepatitis with jaundice, a yellow-coated tongue taking imprint of teeth, foul breath and night sweats in a mercurial constitution suggest:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Mercurius: imprints of teeth, offensive breath and sweat.

Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Human chorionic gonadotropin.
Signs of dehydration in a child with diarrhoea include sunken eyes, thirst and:
Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Skin pinch goes back slowly.
a diffuse spreading infection of subcutaneous tissue
Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Usually streptococcal.
The best emergency treatment for a chemical splash in the eye is:
immediate copious irrigation with clean water
Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Irrigate for at least 15–20 minutes.
The Pulse Polio campaign aims to give oral polio drops to children under:
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. On National Immunisation Days.
cooling of the body after death

the patient's right to make informed decisions about his or her own care
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. A core principle of medical ethics.
Destructive ulceration, bone pains worse at night and a tendency to deformity are features of which miasm?
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Syphilis: destruction and ulceration, night aggravation.
The ideal prover, according to Hahnemann, is:
healthy, trustworthy and observant of his own sensations
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Provings are done on healthy human beings (§126–127).
The 'law of minimum' (minimum dose) is justified because the sick organism is:
highly sensitive to the similar remedy
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Disease raises susceptibility to the similar stimulus.
Ailments from disappointed love or grief, with weeping alone, aversion to sympathy and a craving for salt, need:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Natrum mur: silent grief.
Delayed, scanty menses, with a mild, weeping disposition, thirstlessness and craving for open air, suggest:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Pulsatilla: changeable, mild, better open air.
Restless anxiety with a fear of death, and the patient predicting the time of death, during a sudden acute illness, suggests:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Aconite predicts the hour of death.
The constitutional remedy of the hydrogenoid constitution (worse from damp) is:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Grauvogl's hydrogenoid constitution.

hard, gritty and only slightly soluble, which aids grinding
Topic 3, Pharmacy. Its hardness helps subdivide the drug.

Topic 3, Pharmacy. It set up the Central Council of Homoeopathy (now replaced by the National Commission for Homoeopathy, 2020).
W. A. Allen's 'Repertory of Intermittent Fevers' is an example of:
Topic 4, Repertory. It deals with one clinical group.
The process of matching the patient's symptoms with the materia medica after repertorisation is called:
final selection by consulting the materia medica
Topic 4, Repertory. The repertory narrows, the materia medica decides.
Which lipoprotein carries cholesterol from the tissues back to the liver (reverse cholesterol transport)?
Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. HDL is protective; desirable 40 mg/dL or more (60 or more protective).
The main buffer of the extracellular fluid is the:
Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Regulated by lungs and kidneys.
Granuloma formation is typically seen in:
Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Chronic granulomatous inflammation.
Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Hansen's bacillus.
Polyuria, polydipsia and weight loss in a young person suggest:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. May present with ketoacidosis.
Dysmenorrhoea with cramping pains relieved by bending double and pressure suggests homoeopathically:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Mag phos is also better from warmth.
Convulsions with the head bent backward (opisthotonos) and violent jerks, especially after a head injury, call for:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Cicuta: opisthotonos, ill effects of concussion.
Rh incompatibility can cause haemolytic disease of the newborn when:
the mother is Rh-negative and the baby Rh-positive
Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Anti-D prophylaxis prevents sensitisation.
The two most important danger signs in a child with cough or difficult breathing are fast breathing and:
Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. IMNCI pneumonia signs.
A 'sprain' is an injury to a:
Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. A strain affects muscle or tendon.
The commonest cause of preventable blindness in India is:
Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Under the National Programme for Control of Blindness.
The specificity of a screening test is its ability to identify correctly:
those who do NOT have the disease
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Sensitivity identifies those with disease.
Ascertaining the time of death from the body includes all EXCEPT:
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Blood group does not change with time.
Euthanasia (passive) in India was permitted with safeguards following the Supreme Court judgment in:
Common Cause v. Union of India (2018)
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Also recognised living wills.
Hahnemann's 'Chronic Diseases' second edition was published in five volumes between:
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The first edition appeared in 1828–1830.
The word 'dynamis' in homoeopathic philosophy refers to:
Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The spirit-like power animating the body.
According to Hahnemann, the most important part of treatment in an epidemic is to:
use the same remedy as the last epidemic
study many cases to find the genus epidemicus
treat each case only with mother tinctures
wait for the epidemic to pass
Effects of mental strain and overwork in students, with brain fag, headache and weak memory, suggest:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Both suit nervous exhaustion from study.
Arterial congestion with a slow pulse, a red streak down the middle of the tongue and convulsions, as in eclampsia, suggest:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Veratrum viride: red streak on the tongue, violent congestion.
Remedies are said to be 'complementary' when:
one completes the action of the other
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Example: Calcarea and Belladonna; Sulphur and Aloe.
Desire to be magnetised, sympathetic nature, fear of thunderstorms and of being alone, and burning pains point to:
Topic 2, Materia Medica. Phosphorus: wants company and sympathy.
Mother tinctures in the HPI are prepared mainly by:
maceration or percolation of the drug in alcohol
Topic 3, Pharmacy. Trituration is for insoluble drugs; succussion makes liquid potencies.
The HPI standard for a homoeopathic drug lays down its:
Topic 3, Pharmacy. Pharmacopoeial monographs fix identity, purity and strength.
The repertory with chapters in the order Mind, Vertigo, Head and so on, following Hahnemann's schema, is:
Topic 4, Repertory. Hahnemannian anatomical schema from head to foot.
The term 'grading' in a repertory refers to:
the value assigned to a remedy in a rubric, shown by typeface
Topic 4, Repertory. Shows how strongly the remedy produced the symptom.
A sudden rise in blood pressure is corrected within seconds mainly by the:
Baroreceptor reflex from the carotid sinus and aortic arch
Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Baroreceptors buffer short-term changes; the kidneys set long-term pressure.
The normal total leucocyte count in adults is:
Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Raised in infection, low in typhoid and dengue.
Haematuria, proteinuria, oedema and hypertension after a sore throat in a child suggest:
Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. One to three weeks after a streptococcal infection.
On abdominal ultrasonography, a gallstone appears as:
an echogenic (bright) focus with posterior acoustic shadowing that moves with posture
a solid mass in the liver
Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Echogenic focus + acoustic shadow + mobility = gallstone.
Pain in the upper abdomen going through to the back, with very high serum amylase, suggests:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Gallstones and alcohol are the main causes.
Allergic rhinitis with violent sneezing, and itching of the palate, worse from the smell of flowers, suggests:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Sabadilla: hay fever.
Sciatica with cramping pain, worse on the left, relieved by heat and pressure, suggests:
Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Colocynth: cramping pains, better pressure.
The ovarian hormone that maintains the endometrium in the second half of the cycle is:
Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. From the corpus luteum.
A newborn's Apgar score is assessed at:
Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Heart rate, breathing, tone, reflex, colour.
Burns of the face and neck are dangerous mainly because of:
Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Early airway assessment is vital.
A painful red lump at the eyelid margin is called a:
Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. A chalazion is usually painless.
raise full immunisation coverage of children and pregnant women
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Launched in 2014.
The poison that causes garlic odour of breath and 'rice-water' stools resembling cholera is:
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Acute arsenic poisoning.
A doctor's duty under the law to inform the police applies to:
medicolegal cases such as injuries, poisoning and suspicious deaths
Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. MLC registration and intimation.
Rodent ulcer is the common name for basal cell carcinoma, which locally erodes tissue.
The first aid to stop external bleeding from a limb wound is:
washing the wound with hot water
applying a cold drink to the lips
firm direct pressure over the wound with a clean pad
Direct pressure with elevation stops most external haemorrhage; a tourniquet is a last resort.
A weak, empty, sinking feeling in the stomach at about 11 a.m. is a keynote of:
Sulphur: faint, empty, weak feeling at 11 a.m. (Allen's Keynotes); Natrum mur is worse at 10 a.m.
Chickenpox with intensely itching vesicles, restlessness and relief from warmth and motion calls for:
Rhus tox suits vesicular eruptions with intense itching and restlessness, better from warmth, as in chickenpox and herpes zoster.
After soaking in the potency, medicated globules should be dried:
in the shade, away from sunlight and strong heat
Heat and sunlight can damage the medicine, so medicated globules are dried in shade at room temperature.
Thuja occidentalis is arbor vitae; savine is Sabina, marsh tea Ledum and yellow jasmine Gelsemium.
A sharp visceral pleural line with no lung markings beyond it on a chest X-ray indicates:
Air in the pleural space separates the visceral pleura from the chest wall, leaving a hyperlucent area without lung markings.
Hahnemann coined 'allopathy' for the system that treats with medicines producing effects different from the disease.
The earliest change of reversible cell injury seen on light microscopy is:
Failure of membrane ion pumps lets water enter the cell, producing cellular swelling, the first and reversible change; nuclear changes indicate irreversible injury.
Skin scrapings are examined for fungal hyphae in suspected dermatophytosis after treatment with:
KOH (10 to 20%) digests keratin so that fungal hyphae can be seen in direct mounts of skin, hair and nail.
The stage of the malaria parasite injected into man by the female Anopheles mosquito is the:
Sporozoites from the mosquito's salivary glands enter the blood and go to the liver to begin exo-erythrocytic schizogony.
On the ECG, the T wave represents:
conduction delay in the AV node
P is atrial depolarisation, QRS ventricular depolarisation and T ventricular repolarisation.
Frequent, ineffectual urging for stool in an irritable, sedentary person who lives on stimulants and rich food calls for:
Nux vomica: frequent ineffectual urging, passing small quantities, in irritable, zealous, sedentary people; Opium and Alumina have no urging.
The antiviral drug used for treating influenza, including H1N1, is:
Oseltamivir is a neuraminidase inhibitor used for influenza A and B, best within 48 hours of onset.
Long before Hahnemann, the idea that disease may be cured by similars was mentioned by:
Hippocrates recognised both contraries and similars as ways of cure; Galen built his system on contraries.
When splinting a suspected fracture of a long bone in first aid, the splint should immobilise:
only the joint below the fracture
the whole body on a stretcher in every case
the joint above and the joint below the fracture
Immobilising the joints on both sides prevents movement of the fragments.
In selecting the homoeopathic remedy, which symptoms are of the least value?
Common pathognomonic symptoms of the disease
Physical generals such as thermal reaction
Pathognomonic symptoms belong to the disease, not the individual, so they rank lowest for remedy selection (§153, Kent).
Graphites is plumbago or black lead; vegetable charcoal is Carbo veg., flint is Silicea and animal charcoal is Carbo animalis.
According to §1 of the Organon, the physician's high and only mission is:
to construct theories about the inner nature of disease
to explain the phenomena of life and disease
to prove medicines on healthy persons
to restore the sick to health, to cure
§1: the physician's high and only mission is to restore the sick to health, to cure, as it is termed; not to spin speculative systems.
Sudden high fever with burning, radiating heat felt by the hand, a bright red face, dilated pupils and throbbing carotids calls for:
Belladonna: suddenness, intense dry heat, redness, throbbing and dilated pupils; Aconite lacks the throbbing congestion and has fear and restlessness.
The pentavalent vaccine in India's UIP protects against diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus and:
hepatitis B and Haemophilus influenzae type b
Pentavalent = DPT + Hep B + Hib, given at 6, 10 and 14 weeks.
Acute cholecystitis is most commonly caused by:
Impaction of a gallstone in the cystic duct
Salmonella infection of the gall bladder
About 90% of acute cholecystitis is calculous, due to a stone obstructing the cystic duct; acalculous disease occurs in the critically ill.
bending of the body to one side
spasmodic arching of the body backwards
spasmodic bending of the body forwards
Opisthotonos is backward arching; forward bending is emprosthotonos and sideways bending pleurothotonos.
The normal platelet count in adults is about:
Normal platelets are 150,000 to 450,000/uL; 4,000 to 11,000 is the WBC range and 4.5 to 5.5 million the RBC count.
In 2020 the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme (RNTCP) was renamed the:
National Programme for Control of Tuberculosis
RNTCP became NTEP in 2020, reflecting the goal of eliminating TB.
The medium routinely used to culture Mycobacterium tuberculosis is:
Thiosulphate citrate bile salt sucrose agar
Egg-based Lowenstein-Jensen medium is the standard solid medium for M. tuberculosis; colonies appear in 2 to 8 weeks.
The third stage of labour extends from:
onset of true labour pains to full cervical dilatation
delivery of the baby to expulsion of the placenta and membranes
full cervical dilatation to delivery of the baby
expulsion of the placenta to one hour after delivery
The third stage is the placental stage; the hour after it is often called the fourth stage (observation).
The mother tincture often used in homoeopathic practice for high blood pressure is:
Rauwolfia Q is used for hypertension; Syzygium is used for diabetes, Blatta for asthma and Berberis for renal colic.
A primigravida usually first perceives fetal movements (quickening) at about:
Quickening is felt at about 20 weeks in a primigravida and about 2 weeks earlier in a multigravida.
Multiple superficial, parallel cuts at the start of a deeper incised wound on the wrist are called hesitation cuts and suggest:
Hesitation (tentative) cuts reflect a trial before the final cut and are typical of suicidal incised wounds.
the contents of the scabies (itch) vesicle
Psorinum is the nosode of the itch vesicle; Syphilinum comes from the chancre.
Aconitum napellus is commonly known as:
Aconitum napellus (Ranunculaceae) is monkshood or wolf's bane; deadly nightshade is Belladonna, foxglove Digitalis and thorn apple Stramonium.
A 'chocolate cyst' of the ovary is characteristic of:
An endometrioma contains old altered blood that looks like chocolate.
The word 'rubric' comes from the Latin for:
red, because old books printed headings in red ink
Rubrica means red; headings were once printed in red, so a repertory heading is a rubric.
According to §2, the highest ideal of cure is:
removal of the most troublesome symptom as quickly as possible
palliation of suffering until the disease runs its natural course
removal of the material cause of disease by evacuation
rapid, gentle and permanent restoration of health on easily comprehensible principles
§2 defines the ideal cure as rapid, gentle and permanent restoration of health, or removal of the disease in its whole extent, in the shortest, most reliable and most harmless way.
Kent, following Swedenborg, described the vital force as:
Kent's Lectures on Homoeopathic Philosophy call the vital force 'simple substance', an immaterial substance with formative intelligence.
Hyperthyroidism with emaciation despite a ravenous appetite, anxiety when hungry, relief from eating and intolerance of heat, calls for:
Iodum patients lose flesh while eating well, feel better after eating and are warm-blooded; it is used for goitre and thyrotoxicosis.
A net reproduction rate (NRR) of 1 means that:
each woman bears exactly one child
the population is doubling every generation
each generation of mothers is exactly replaced by an equal number of daughters
the birth rate equals 1 per 1,000 population
NRR = 1 is replacement-level fertility, roughly equal to a TFR of about 2.1.
An infarct in which of the following organs typically undergoes liquefactive necrosis?
Ischaemic death of CNS tissue produces liquefactive necrosis; infarcts of other solid organs show coagulative necrosis.
According to §§74 and 75, the most deplorable and incurable of all chronic diseases are those produced by:
§75: artificial chronic diseases caused by allopathic treatment are the most deplorable and incurable of all.
In measles, the rash typically appears on about the:
1st day of fever, on the trunk
2nd day of fever, on the palms and soles
4th day of fever, starting behind the ears and along the hairline
7th day of fever, on the abdomen
The maculopapular measles rash appears around day 4, starting behind the ears and at the hairline, then spreading downwards.
A thin, breathless COPD patient with pursed-lip breathing, a hyperinflated chest and near-normal blood gases until late is described as a:
Emphysema-dominant patients hyperventilate to keep oxygenation ('pink puffers'); bronchitis-dominant patients are hypoxic, cyanosed and oedematous ('blue bloaters').
Low serum T4 with a high TSH indicates:
A failing thyroid removes negative feedback, so the pituitary raises TSH; in pituitary failure both T4 and TSH are low.
A fastidious, exacting patient who cannot bear disorder, with burning pains relieved by heat, needs:
Arsenicum album is the classic fastidious remedy, with burning pains better by heat and restless anxiety.
Under IMNCI, fast breathing in a child aged 2 to 12 months is a respiratory rate of:
Cut-offs are 60/min under 2 months, 50/min for 2–12 months and 40/min for 1–5 years.
Excessive scar tissue that grows beyond the margins of the original wound and does not regress is called a:
A keloid extends beyond the wound boundary and seldom regresses; a hypertrophic scar stays within the wound margins.
Diseases such as smallpox, measles and whooping cough, which recur in the same manner and attack a person usually only once in life, are called in §73:
§73 groups acute diseases into individual, sporadic, epidemic and acute miasms; smallpox and measles are acute miasms of fixed character.
According to §141, the best of all provings are those made by:
the healthy, unprejudiced and sensitive physician on himself
students under the supervision of a professor
volunteers who know nothing of the drug
§141: the best pure experiments are those the healthy, unprejudiced, sensitive physician makes on himself.
Suspicion, secretiveness, jealousy and fixed ideas are the mental features of which miasm?
Sycotic mentals are suspicious, secretive, jealous and fixed in ideas; psora is anxious and fearful, syphilis destructive and depressed.
Phatak's Concise Repertory of Homoeopathic Medicines was built mainly on:
S. R. Phatak based his alphabetical repertory chiefly on C. M. Boger's Synoptic Key, enlarging it from other sources.
While a woman is on magnesium sulphate, the first clinical sign of toxicity to watch for is:
Knee jerk disappears at serum levels around 10 mEq/L, before respiratory depression; so the reflex is checked before every repeat dose.
In Kent's eighth observation, patients who prove every remedy they receive are:
oversensitive, idiosyncratic patients who are often incurable
patients who need repeated high doses
patients with a purely acute disease
Kent: some patients prove every remedy; they are oversensitive and idiosyncratic, and such cases are often incurable; lower potencies are used.
Acute fright and fear of death immediately after an accident, with great anxiety and restlessness, calls for:
Aconite suits sudden, violent shock with intense fear of death.
Long-standing PCOS with chronic anovulation increases the risk of:
Unopposed oestrogen without progesterone leads to endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma.
Hahnemann's Calcarea carbonica is prepared from:
native chalk dug from the earth
the outer dark layer of the oyster shell
the middle, snow-white layer of the oyster shell
Calcarea carbonica (Calcarea ostrearum) is the impure calcium carbonate of the middle snow-white layer of the oyster shell.
Hahnemann's first index of symptoms appeared as Part 2 of:
the first edition of the Organon
The second part of the Fragmenta (1805) was an index of symptoms, the forerunner of the repertory.
A type I (alpha) error in hypothesis testing is:
rejecting a null hypothesis that is actually true
accepting a null hypothesis that is actually false
Type I error is a false positive conclusion (rejecting a true null hypothesis); accepting a false null hypothesis is a type II error.
Under standard pre-anaesthetic fasting guidelines for an elective adult operation, clear fluids may be taken up to:
Usual rules: clear fluids 2 h, breast milk 4 h, light meal or non-human milk 6 h.
In hepatitis B infection, the serum marker indicating active viral replication and high infectivity is:
HBeAg correlates with high levels of HBV DNA and infectivity; seroconversion to anti-HBe indicates reduced replication.
On abdominal ultrasonography, fatty liver typically appears as a liver with:
A shrunken nodular outline with ascites
Fat in hepatocytes increases reflectivity, so the liver looks brighter than the kidney cortex; a small nodular liver with ascites suggests cirrhosis.
The pain of primary dysmenorrhoea is mainly due to excess endometrial production of:
PGF2α causes myometrial hypercontractility and ischaemia, which is why NSAIDs relieve it.
The main lung volumes that add up to the vital capacity are:
tidal volume + inspiratory reserve volume only
inspiratory reserve volume + tidal volume + expiratory reserve volume
Vital capacity is the maximum air that can be expired after a maximal inspiration: IRV + TV + ERV (about 4.5–4.8 L).
Tablets used in homoeopathy are made of:
Homoeopathic tablets are pressed from lactose; globules and pilules are made of cane sugar.
A Smith's fracture is a fracture of the distal radius with:
volar (anterior) displacement of the distal fragment
dorsal displacement of the distal fragment
fracture of the ulnar styloid only
Smith's fracture is the 'reversed Colles'', caused by a fall on the back of the flexed wrist.
Kent held that menstrual state expresses the woman as a whole, so he ranked menstrual symptoms as generals.
Burns and scalds with raw, smarting pain, relieved by cold applications, especially before blisters form, call for:
Cantharis is the leading remedy for burns and scalds, given before blisters form.
The abbreviation 'gtt.' on a prescription stands for:
Gtt. is short for guttae, drops.
The most consistent biochemical finding in nutritional rickets is:
Alkaline phosphatase rises with osteoblastic activity; phosphate is low and PTH high.
excessively particular about neatness and details
Fastidious patients, such as Arsenicum, insist on order and exactness in small things.
In Kent's Repertory, the rubric for constipation is in the chapter:
Constipation and diarrhoea are rubrics of Rectum; Stool describes the character of the stool itself.
According to §108, the peculiar effects of medicines on human health can be ascertained only by:
giving them experimentally in moderate doses to healthy persons
observing their effects in the sick
chemical analysis of the drug substance
§108: there is no other way than to administer medicines experimentally to healthy persons.
high anion gap metabolic acidosis with deep, rapid (Kussmaul) breathing
Ketoacids add unmeasured anions, widening the anion gap; the lungs compensate by blowing off CO₂.
Horrock's apparatus is used to find:
the dose of bleaching powder needed to disinfect well water
Horrock's apparatus estimates the amount of bleaching powder needed to give a free residual chlorine in water.
In Kent's Repertory, symptoms of the nails are found in the chapter:
Nails are listed as part of the extremities, for example 'Extremities, Nails, brittle'.
The total leucocyte count in uncomplicated typhoid fever typically shows:
Typhoid characteristically causes leucopenia with relative lymphocytosis and absent eosinophils; leucocytosis suggests a complication such as perforation.
An impulse to jump down when crossing a bridge or standing in a high place calls for:
Argentum nitricum: on a high place or bridge, the thought of jumping off; fear of high buildings (Boericke).
Chamomilla (Matricaria chamomilla) belongs to which plant family?
Chamomilla, like Arnica, belongs to the Compositae; Belladonna is Solanaceae, Aconite Ranunculaceae and Nux vomica Loganiaceae.
Angina with a sensation as if the heart were grasped by an iron hand, worse lying on the left side, calls for:
Constriction 'as if by an iron band or hand' around the heart and chest is the keynote of Cactus grandiflorus.
In Kent's Repertory, palpitation of the heart is looked up in the chapter:
Kent has no Heart chapter; palpitation and heart symptoms sit in Chest.
Which of the following is a specific treponemal test for syphilis?
TPHA detects antibodies against Treponema pallidum antigens; VDRL, RPR and Kahn are non-treponemal tests using cardiolipin.
White blood cell casts in urine are characteristic of:
WBC casts form in the tubules and so localise inflammation to the kidney, as in pyelonephritis; cystitis gives pus cells without casts.
The abbreviation 'p.c.' on a prescription means:
P.c. is post cibum, after food.
Religious mania with a desire to cut and tear things, and cold sweat on the forehead, points to:
Veratrum album: religious mania, destructive impulses to cut and tear, with cold sweat on the forehead (Boericke).
Tissue bridges, ragged margins and bruised edges in a wound indicate a:
A laceration is a tear from blunt force, leaving nerves and vessels as tissue bridges; incised wounds have clean edges.
The abbreviation 'q.s.' on a prescription means:
Q.s. is quantum sufficit, as much as is needed; 'as much as desired' is ad lib.
Volkmann's ischaemic contracture is a classic complication of:
supracondylar fracture of the humerus in children
fracture of the shaft of the femur
Brachial artery injury or compression in supracondylar fracture causes forearm muscle ischaemia and contracture.
In Kent's sixth observation, too short a relief of symptoms after a remedy points to:
organic (structural) changes or something interfering with the remedy
a remedy that was too deep for the case
Kent: amelioration that lasts too short a time suggests structural change in the organs, or in acute cases a rapidly advancing process.
In active management of the third stage of labour, the uterotonic of choice is:
ergometrine 0.5 mg IV before delivery of the shoulder
misoprostol 1000 mcg rectally after the placenta
oxytocin 10 IU IM within one minute of birth
WHO and Indian guidelines recommend oxytocin 10 IU IM as the first-choice uterotonic for AMTSL.
A potency labelled '200K' has been prepared by:
The suffix K marks potencies made by Korsakov's single-vial method.
Before the HPI was published, Indian manufacturers mainly followed:
the American (HPUS) and German homoeopathic pharmacopoeias
the Indian Pharmacopoeia of allopathic drugs
Until the HPI appeared, Indian firms worked to the Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia of the United States and the German pharmacopoeia.
Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016, used hypodermic needles and scalpel blades go into the:
Sharps, including needles, syringes with fixed needles and blades, go into the white translucent puncture-proof container.
In healing by second intention, closure of the wound gap is helped chiefly by:
fibrin glue formed in the first hour
Large open wounds fill with granulation tissue and shrink through myofibroblast contraction.
In a typhoid state, the patient can swallow only liquids, as the least solid food causes gagging; the remedy is:
Baptisia: painless sore throat, can swallow liquids only, the least solid food gags (Boericke, Allen).
In adults, the paranasal sinus most commonly involved in sinusitis is the:
The maxillary sinus is most often affected in adults; the ethmoids are most often affected in children.
The name of the software RADAR stands for:
Rapid Aid to Drug Aimed Research
Rapid Analysis of Disease And Remedy
RADAR, from Archibel in Belgium, is short for Rapid Aid to Drug Aimed Research.
A dry, spasmodic cough at night that is worse on lying down and relieved by sitting up, in a jealous, suspicious patient, suggests:
Hyoscyamus: dry nocturnal cough worse lying down, better sitting up (Boericke).
Irregular, spasmodic false labour pains that fly about the abdomen, with a rigid os and great exhaustion, call for:
Caulophyllum is the classic remedy for spasmodic, ineffectual pains with rigidity of the os and weakness.
The most specific serum marker of myocardial injury is:
Troponins are specific to heart muscle and stay raised for days; CK-MB, AST and LDH are less specific.
The birth dose of hepatitis B vaccine under the UIP should be given:
any time in the first year
Hep B birth dose is effective in preventing perinatal transmission only if given within 24 hours.
Regarding a dying declaration recorded by a doctor, which statement is correct?
The accused must be present and may cross-examine
It is valid only if recorded by a magistrate
It must be made in the presence of a police officer
No oath is given, and the doctor should certify that the declarant was conscious and of sound mind
A dying declaration needs no oath and no presence of the accused; the doctor certifies compos mentis. The dying deposition, with the accused present, is recorded by a magistrate.
cells of the proximal convoluted tubule
juxtaglomerular cells of the afferent arteriole
The juxtaglomerular (granular) cells secrete renin; the macula densa senses tubular NaCl and signals them.
Hahnemann held (§119) that one medicine can never be a substitute (succedaneum) for another because:
medicines from the same family act alike
only the dose decides the action
substitutes are forbidden by the law of potency
every medicine has its own peculiar and distinct action
§119: as every plant species differs, each medicine has a distinct action, so none can replace another.
Convulsions with opisthotonus and risus sardonicus, with the mind clear between the fits, suggest poisoning by:
Strychnine blocks glycine inhibition in the spinal cord, causing tetanic convulsions while consciousness is preserved between fits.
Pancreatic trypsinogen is activated in the duodenum by:
Enterokinase from the duodenal mucosa converts trypsinogen to trypsin, which then activates the other pancreatic proenzymes.
Fever with conjunctival suffusion, calf tenderness, jaundice and acute kidney injury after wading in flood water during the monsoon suggests:
Weil's disease is the icteric, haemorrhagic and renal form of leptospirosis; conjunctival suffusion and calf tenderness are typical.
In acute diseases (§§262 and 263), the patient's craving for particular food and drink should generally be:
gratified within reason, as it comes from the instinct of the vital force
strictly refused, as it may antidote the remedy
replaced by a fixed hospital diet
satisfied only after the fever subsides
§262–263: in acute disease the desires of the patient, guided by the vital force, should not be opposed, though a slight gratification of palliative wishes is enough.
Prolapse of the rectum before or with the stool, with profuse gushing diarrhoea, is characteristic of:
Podophyllum: prolapsus ani before or with stool (Boericke, Allen).
Hypertension with hypokalaemia, metabolic alkalosis and suppressed plasma renin, without Cushingoid features, most suggests:
Autonomous aldosterone excess causes sodium retention, potassium loss and alkalosis, with renin suppressed; renal artery stenosis raises renin.
the venom of the honey bee
the contents of a scabies vesicle
the sputum of a tuberculous patient
Pyrogenium (artificial sepsin) is made from lean beef allowed to decompose in water.
In the liver, bilirubin is made water-soluble by conjugation with:
UDP-glucuronyl transferase conjugates bilirubin with glucuronic acid; albumin only carries unconjugated bilirubin in plasma.
Multiple, recurrent peptic ulcers including in the jejunum, with diarrhoea and very high gastric acid output, suggest a:
Gastrin from a pancreatic or duodenal gastrinoma drives massive acid secretion, causing refractory ulcers at unusual sites and diarrhoea.
Impaired glucose tolerance is defined by a 2-hour plasma glucose, after a 75 g oral glucose load, of:
A 2-hour value of 140 to 199 mg/dL is IGT, 200 or more is diabetes; 100 to 125 mg/dL fasting defines impaired fasting glucose.
A very high blood pressure is termed a hypertensive emergency, rather than urgency, when there is:
A diastolic BP above 120 mmHg without symptoms
Failure to respond to three antihypertensive drugs
A hypertensive emergency is severe BP elevation with acute organ damage (encephalopathy, LVF, dissection, AKI); without it the situation is urgency.
In the WHO oral glucose tolerance test, an adult is given:
The standard OGTT uses 75 g of anhydrous glucose; a 2-hour value of 200 mg/dL or more indicates diabetes.
Winging of the scapula on pushing against a wall is due to injury of the:
The long thoracic nerve (C5–C7) supplies serratus anterior, which holds the scapula against the chest wall.
The Declaration of Helsinki (1964) of the World Medical Association deals with:
ethical principles for medical research involving human subjects
the determination of the time of death
Helsinki covers research on human subjects; Tokyo (1975) torture, Sydney (1968) death, Geneva (1948) the oath.
Marjolin's ulcer is a malignant change in a long-standing scar or chronic ulcer, and is histologically a:
Marjolin's ulcer is a slow-growing squamous cell carcinoma arising in burn scars or chronic ulcers.
Recurrent styes and chalazia on the eyelids, in a sensitive person with suppressed indignation, call for:
Staphisagria: styes and chalazia one after another (Boericke), with the background of suppressed anger.
Irritable bowel with diarrhoea from anticipation before an event, craving for sweets that disagree, and flatulence with loud belching calls for:
Anticipatory anxiety, craving for sweets that aggravate, and loud explosive belching are keynotes of Argentum nitricum.
Caries of the nasal and palatine bones, with ozaena and a putrid smell from the nose, in a depressed syphilitic patient suggests:
Aurum met: caries of nasal and palatine bones, ozaena, putrid odour (Boericke), with profound melancholy.
In 'The Genius of Homoeopathy', Stuart Close defined susceptibility as:
the tendency of a disease to spread in a community
the power of a drug to produce symptoms in the healthy
the general quality of the living organism of receiving impressions, the power to react to stimuli
the strength of the medicine after potentisation
Close: susceptibility is the capability of the living organism to receive impressions and react to stimuli; it governs both cure and the choice of dose.
Constant nausea in pregnancy not relieved by vomiting, with a clean tongue, calls for:
Persistent nausea unrelieved by vomiting with a clean tongue is the keynote of Ipecac; Nux and Ant crud have coated tongues.
Weakness and backache, as if the back would break, with sweating, after labour or abortion, call for:
Kali carb: backache, sweat and weakness after confinement or miscarriage (Allen's Keynotes, Boericke).
A rubbery intravascular clot with a dark-red dependent 'currant-jelly' part and a yellow 'chicken-fat' upper part, not attached to the vessel wall, is a:
Post-mortem clots form after death as red cells settle, giving currant-jelly and chicken-fat layers; they lack lines of Zahn and wall attachment.
Aethusa cynapium is commonly known as:
Aethusa cynapium is fool's parsley (Umbelliferae); wind flower is Pulsatilla, poison nut Nux vomica and bitter-sweet Dulcamara.
A timid child who hides behind furniture when strangers come, and whose tonsils inflame and suppurate with every cold, needs:
Baryta carb: bashful child hides behind furniture; quinsy and tonsillitis after every cold (Boericke).
In chronic osteomyelitis, a piece of dead bone separated from living bone is called the:
The sequestrum is dead bone; the involucrum is new bone around it; cloacae are openings in the involucrum.
According to §138, the changes of health that a prover feels during the action of the medicine are:
to be regarded as derived solely from that medicine
to be ignored unless they are new to him
to be regarded as his own latent disease
to be recorded only if confirmed in animals
§138: all sufferings and changes during the proving, under proper conditions, belong to the medicine and are recorded as its symptoms.
In Kent's Repertory, dreams are found in the chapter:
Kent has no separate Dreams chapter; dreams are a rubric under Sleep.
Thick, horny callosities on the soles, split nails and a sentimental mood in the moonlight indicate:
Antimonium crudum: horny callosities and warts, cracked nails, sentimental in moonlight (Boericke).
Under Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK), children are screened for defects at birth, diseases, deficiencies and:
RBSK screens children aged 0-18 years for the '4 Ds': defects at birth, diseases, deficiencies and developmental delays including disability.
Bed-wetting in an irritable child who picks at the nose, grinds the teeth in sleep and has a canine hunger calls for:
Cina is the classic worm remedy with nose-boring, teeth grinding, ravenous hunger and nocturnal enuresis.
Anaemia with pallor, in which the face flushes fiery red on the least emotion or exertion (false plethora), calls for:
Ferrum met: anaemic yet with false plethora; face flushes red on the least pain, emotion or exertion (Allen's Keynotes).
Preventing the emergence of risk factors (such as unhealthy diets) in a population where they have not yet appeared is called:
Primordial prevention acts before risk factors arise, mainly by health education and lifestyle change in children.
Kent's Repertory contains how many chapters?
Kent's Repertory runs in 37 chapters, from Mind to Generalities.
Enlarged red cells containing Schuffner's dots on a peripheral smear are seen in infection with:
P. vivax (and P. ovale) infect young red cells, which enlarge and show Schuffner's dots; P. falciparum shows Maurer's clefts.
The 'Bolam test' in medical negligence holds that a doctor is not negligent if:
the patient had signed a written consent form
he acted in accordance with a practice accepted as proper by a responsible body of fellow practitioners
the outcome of the treatment was favourable
he had charged no fee for the treatment
Bolam v. Friern Hospital (1957): the standard of care is that of a responsible body of skilled practitioners in that field.
Sinusitis with thick, tough, stringy, yellow-green discharge and pain at the root of the nose calls for:
Ropy, stringy discharge with pressure pain at the root of the nose is the keynote of Kali bichromicum.
Burning pains relieved by heat, or a dry mouth without thirst, are examples of:
They contradict what is expected, which makes them peculiar symptoms of high value (Organon §153).
The dependency ratio is calculated as:
population aged 65 and above / total population
The dependency ratio relates the economically dependent young and old to the working-age population of 15-64 years.
The second booster of DPT vaccine under the UIP is given at:
DPT booster-1 is at 16–24 months and booster-2 at 5–6 years; Td follows at 10 and 16 years.
'Relationship of Remedies and Sides of the Body', a standard reference on complementary and inimical remedies, was written by:
R. Gibson Miller's small book lists the complementary, inimical, antidotal and following remedies, and the sides of the body each affects.
Headache of schoolchildren, especially girls at puberty, in thin, growing children is characteristic of:
Calcarea phos: headache of school girls, with growing pains and slow bone development (Boericke).
Antidiuretic hormone and oxytocin are synthesised in the:
supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei of the hypothalamus
They are made in hypothalamic neurons, carried down their axons and stored in and released from the posterior pituitary.
A hypothyroid woman with a firm, painless goitre and strongly positive anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies most likely has:
Hashimoto's autoimmune thyroiditis, with anti-TPO antibodies, is the commonest cause of hypothyroidism in iodine-sufficient areas.
Which of these is a feature of LIFE-THREATENING acute asthma?
A silent chest, cyanosis, SpO2 below 92%, PEF below 33% and exhaustion mark life-threatening asthma; HR 110 and RR 25 mark acute severe asthma.
Deep depression with suicidal thoughts, mental dullness and destructive impulses are the mental features of which miasm?
The syphilitic miasm is destructive both in tissue and mind: depression, dullness, suicidal and destructive tendencies.
Camphor is known in homoeopathy as an antidote to:
Camphor antidotes the action of most vegetable remedies, so it is kept away from patients under treatment.
A fixed pain under the inferior angle of the right scapula, with liver complaints and jaundice, calls for the organ remedy:
Chelidonium: constant pain under the lower inner angle of the right scapula is its keynote; it is a leading liver remedy.
Skin eruptions with deep, bleeding cracks that are worse in winter, together with seasickness, point to:
Petroleum: deep fissures and cracks worse in winter; nausea from riding in carriages and ships (Boericke).
The specific antidote for paracetamol overdose is:
N-acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione and prevents liver necrosis.
After digestion, long-chain fatty acids leave the intestinal cells mainly as:
fatty acids bound to albumin in the hepatic artery
free fatty acids entering the portal vein
Long-chain fats are re-esterified and packed into chylomicrons, which enter the lymph via lacteals; short-chain fatty acids go to the portal blood.
After about 24 hours of fasting, blood glucose is maintained mainly by:
absorption of glucose from the gut
release of free glucose from muscle glycogen
Liver glycogen is largely used up within about a day; muscle lacks glucose-6-phosphatase and cannot release free glucose.
Culture of faeces in typhoid fever is most often positive during the:
Blood culture is positive in the first week, Widal from the second, and stool culture mainly in the third and fourth weeks ('BASU' sequence).
A competitive inhibitor of an enzyme:
lowers Vmax but leaves Km unchanged
raises Vmax but leaves Km unchanged
raises the apparent Km but leaves Vmax unchanged
The inhibitor competes for the active site, so more substrate is needed for half-maximal velocity, but enough substrate still reaches the same Vmax.
Pure motor hemiparesis of face, arm and leg without aphasia, visual field loss or sensory deficit in a long-standing hypertensive suggests:
Lacunar infarcts from hypertensive small-vessel disease in the internal capsule cause pure motor or pure sensory strokes without cortical signs.
A woman with uterine haemorrhage who finds music intolerable, as it makes her nervous, needs:
Sabina (Boericke): music is intolerable and produces nervousness; uterine bleeding with pain from sacrum to pubis.
In Poonam Verma v. Ashwin Patel (1996), the Supreme Court held that a homoeopath prescribing allopathic drugs without the required qualification is:
protected under the Consumer Protection Act
guilty only if the patient dies
not negligent if the drug is commonly used
Practising a system of medicine without qualification in it was held to be negligence per se.
A deep-vein thrombus that reaches the systemic arterial circulation through a patent foramen ovale is called:
Paradoxical (crossed) embolism occurs when a venous embolus passes through an interatrial or interventricular defect into the systemic arteries.
The earliest clinical sign of rickets in a young infant is:
Craniotabes (ping-pong softening of the skull) appears in early infancy; rosary and limb deformities come later.
In the Asiatic cholera epidemic of 1831, the remedy Hahnemann advised for the first stage was:
Hahnemann advised Camphor in the first stage and Cuprum or Veratrum album in the later stages of cholera.
A fever patient who must be covered in every stage, because he becomes chilly on the slightest uncovering or movement even during the heat, needs:
Nux vomica: chilliness in all stages of fever; cannot move or uncover without feeling chilly (Allen's Keynotes).
A gastric ulcer that is round and 'punched out', with pain felt in a small spot, calls for:
Kali bich has deep, round, punched-out ulcers on mucous membranes and pains in small spots that can be covered with a fingertip.
Chest pain at rest, often in the early morning, with transient ST-segment elevation that settles with nitrates and normal troponin, is typical of:
Variant angina results from coronary artery spasm, giving transient ST elevation at rest; pericarditis gives widespread, persistent concave ST elevation.
An ulcer with a punched-out edge, as if cut with a punch, is typical of a:
Punched-out edges are seen in gummatous (and trophic) ulcers; TB is undermined, SCC everted, BCC rolled.
Long-term corticosteroid therapy must be tapered rather than stopped abruptly because:
the kidneys can no longer excrete potassium
the steroids have permanently destroyed the pituitary
negative feedback has suppressed CRH and ACTH, and the adrenal cortex has atrophied
the liver has stopped making cortisol-binding globulin
Exogenous steroid suppresses the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis; abrupt withdrawal can cause acute adrenal insufficiency.
Inability to pass urine in the presence of others is characteristic of:
Natrum mur (Allen's Keynotes): cannot pass urine in the presence of others.
Sulphur is listed as complementary to which remedy for rectal complaints and diarrhoea?
Boericke: Aloe – complementary Sulphur; and Sulphur's complementaries include Aloe and Psorinum.
A headache that is relieved by the passing of a profuse quantity of urine is characteristic of:
Gelsemium: headache relieved by profuse urination (Allen's Keynotes, Boericke).
Indifference towards those he loves best, with a buoyant feeling and an increased ability to exert himself without fatigue, suggests:
Fluoric acid (Boericke): indifference towards those loved best; increased ability to exercise mentally and physically without fatigue.
The police inquest, formerly under CrPC section 174, is now covered by:
BNSS 194 replaces CrPC 174 (police inquest); BNSS 196 replaces CrPC 176 (magistrate inquest).
In Boenninghausen's seven-point scheme (Quis, Quid, Ubi, Quibus auxiliis, Cur, Quomodo, Quando), 'Quibus auxiliis' refers to:
Quibus auxiliis ('with what help') means the concomitants; Cur is the cause, Quando the time and Ubi the seat.
Mallory-Denk bodies (Mallory hyaline) in hepatocytes are most characteristic of:
Mallory hyaline consists of damaged intermediate (keratin) filaments and is a hallmark of alcoholic hepatitis; apoptotic Councilman bodies occur in viral hepatitis.
Jaundice with an enlarged, tender liver, clay-coloured stools and a tendency to gallstones, for which the mother tincture is often used, calls for:
Chionanthus is a liver remedy for jaundice, hepatic enlargement, clay-coloured stools and gallstone colic.
Under the current UIP, fractional IPV (fIPV, 0.1 mL intradermal) is given at:
Since 2023 a third fIPV dose at 9 months has been added to the 6- and 14-week doses.
On a standard ECG recorded at 25 mm/s, the R–R interval is 4 large squares. The heart rate is about:
Each large square is 0.2 s; heart rate = 300 ÷ number of large squares = 300 ÷ 4 = 75/min.
Jaundice persisting beyond two weeks in an infant with pale clay-coloured stools and dark urine most suggests:
Conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia with acholic stools points to biliary atresia, which needs surgery (Kasai) before 8 weeks.
According to Kent, if the first prescription has produced no action at all, the next prescription is:
always a repetition of the same remedy in a higher potency
not a second prescription, but really a first prescription again
Kent: the second prescription is the one that follows a prescription that has acted; if the first did nothing, the next is still a first prescription.
A patient says she always feels guilty, as if she had committed some crime. The most suitable Kent rubric is:
Mind, Delusions, persecuted, that he is
Mind, Anxiety, conscience, of (as if guilty of a crime)
Kent's rubric 'Anxiety of conscience, as if guilty of a crime' converts this expression exactly.
Lientery is the passing of food undigested in the stool.
Radical cure of Plasmodium vivax malaria under the Indian national programme requires, after G6PD consideration:
Primaquine (0.25 mg/kg daily for 14 days) kills the liver hypnozoites that cause relapse; chloroquine treats only the blood stage.
Metformin is contraindicated when the eGFR falls below:
Because of the risk of lactic acidosis, metformin is stopped below an eGFR of 30, and the dose is reviewed or reduced between 30 and 45.
The population norm for one Primary Health Centre in hilly, tribal or difficult areas is:
A PHC covers 30,000 in plains and 20,000 in hilly or tribal areas; 80,000 is the CHC norm for hilly areas.
A lesion of the primary visual cortex of one occipital lobe typically produces:
total blindness of the eye on the same side
contralateral homonymous hemianopia with macular sparing
The visual cortex receives the opposite half-field of both eyes; the macula is often spared owing to dual blood supply. Bitemporal loss is from the optic chiasma.
Which remedy is inimical to Mercurius and should not follow it?
Boericke lists Silicea as incompatible with Mercurius; Hepar is its antidote.
Haemoglobin in a large adult sample is normally distributed with mean 12 g/dL and standard deviation 1 g/dL. About what proportion lies between 10 and 14 g/dL?
10-14 is mean +/- 2 SD, which covers about 95% of a normal distribution; +/- 1 SD covers 68%.
According to §270, the vial in which an LM potency is succussed should be filled to about:
Hahnemann specified a vial two-thirds full, leaving room for the liquid to be struck forcefully during the 100 succussions.
Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) 2023, hurt that causes severe bodily pain or inability to follow ordinary pursuits is grievous when it lasts for at least:
BNS section 116 reduced the period from the 20 days of IPC 320 to 15 days.
MacRepertory, which uses the Complete Repertory, was created by:
MacRepertory is David Warkentin's software; van Zandvoort compiled the Complete Repertory used in it.
The earliest and most reliable sign of an impending compartment syndrome is:
severe pain on passive stretching of the muscles
Pain out of proportion and on passive stretch comes first; loss of pulse is a late sign.
Inflammation of the mastoid, with swelling and pain behind the ear, in a fat, chilly, homesick patient, calls for:
Capsicum is a classic remedy for mastoiditis (Boericke: swelling and pain behind the ears, inflammation of the mastoid).
Primary prophylaxis against bleeding from large oesophageal varices in cirrhosis can be given with a non-selective beta-blocker such as:
Non-selective beta-blockers (propranolol, nadolol, carvedilol) lower portal pressure by reducing cardiac output and splanchnic flow; cardioselective atenolol does not.
Within a rubric of Kent's Repertory, the sub-rubrics are arranged in the order:
character, location, extension, conditions, time, side
side, time, conditions (modalities), extension, location, character
location, sensation, modality, concomitant, time, side
time, side, location, extension, character, conditions
