Kent's fixed plan: sides first, then time, then modalities, then extension, then location and finally the character of the sensation.
In a cohort study, the incidence of lung cancer among smokers minus that among non-smokers gives the:
Attributable risk is the difference in incidence between exposed and non-exposed; it shows how much disease could be prevented by removing the exposure. Relative risk is the ratio.
According to Kent's ninth observation, what does a well-conducted proving generally do to a healthy prover?
It makes the prover more susceptible to all diseases
It has no effect when high potencies are used
Kent's ninth observation: provers in good health are usually benefited, and sensitive provers may even be cured of latent troubles, by careful provings.
Prolonged bleeding time with a low platelet count but normal PT and aPTT in an otherwise well child after a viral illness suggests:
Isolated thrombocytopenia prolongs bleeding time while coagulation tests stay normal; haemophilia prolongs aPTT, and vitamin K deficiency and DIC prolong PT.
The concept of organ remedies (organopathy), derived from Rademacher, was developed in homoeopathy chiefly by:
J. Compton Burnett popularised organ remedies, such as Ceanothus for the spleen and Chelidonium for the liver, building on Rademacher.
The functional residual capacity is the sum of:
FRC is the air left in the lungs at the end of a quiet expiration: ERV + RV (about 2.3–2.5 L).
Hahnemann's 'Fragmenta de viribus medicamentorum positivis' (1805), the first collection of provings, contained:
Fragmenta de viribus (1805), written in Latin, recorded the provings of 27 drugs.
In the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, 'homoeopathic medicines' are defined in Rule:
Rule 2(dd) defines homoeopathic medicines; Rule 30AA deals with import and Rule 67A with sale.
Which of the following is NOT one of the seven sections of Boenninghausen's Therapeutic Pocket Book?
TPB's sections are mind, parts of the body, sensations and complaints, sleep and dreams, fever, aggravations and ameliorations, and relationship; it has no disease section.
Fibrinoid necrosis of arteriolar walls is characteristic of:
Fibrinoid necrosis is seen in immune-mediated vasculitis and in malignant hypertension, where fibrin leaks into damaged arteriolar walls.
Hair that tangles at the tips and sticks together so that it cannot be combed (plica polonica) is a keynote of:
Borax: hair frowzy and tangled, splits and sticks together at the tips (Boericke, Allen).
Tenderness in the anatomical snuffbox after a fall on the outstretched hand suggests a fracture of the scaphoid, whose feared complication is:
avascular necrosis of the proximal fragment
The scaphoid's blood supply enters distally, so the proximal pole may lose its supply and necrose.
Which remedy is regarded as the chronic of Apis mellifica?
Natrum muriaticum is the chronic of Apis, as it is of Ignatia.
The 1 : 50,000 ratio of each LM step arises because:
one drop is added to 100 drops of alcohol, and one medicated globule carries about 1/500 of a drop
fifty succussions are given to a 1:1000 dilution
each step adds one drop to 500 drops and gives 100 succussions
one grain is diluted in 50,000 grains of lactose
A drop moistens about 500 globules, so one globule holds about 1/500 drop; dissolving it and adding 100 drops gives 1/100 × 1/500 = 1/50,000.
In Kent's Repertory, yawning is found in the chapter:
Kent places yawning under Sleep, alongside sleepiness and sleeplessness.
In a chronic case where the patient has been taking medicines up to the time of the visit, §91 advises the physician to:
record the case at once, as the drug symptoms are part of the disease
continue the old medicines and add the homoeopathic remedy
leave him some days without medicine before taking the final picture
antidote the old medicines immediately with Nux vomica
§91: symptoms during a course of medicine do not give the pure picture; in chronic cases the patient may be left a few days without medicine.
Hilton's method of draining an abscess in the axilla or neck involves:
deep sharp incision straight into the cavity
incising the skin and opening the cavity with blunt sinus forceps
complete excision of the abscess wall
Blunt opening after a skin incision avoids injury to the important vessels and nerves nearby.
Mental symptoms such as depression or irritability arising as ill effects of a head injury call for:
Natrum sulph is known for chronic mental effects of injuries to the head.
In the 6th edition of the Organon, §248 advises that the medicinal solution be:
succussed a few times before each dose, so that each dose is slightly altered in potency
kept unshaken so that every dose has exactly the same potency
diluted 1:100 in fresh alcohol before each dose
§248 directs that the bottle be given several succussions before each dose, so repeated doses are not identical and are better tolerated.
A major limitation of card repertories is that they:
need a computer to read the cards
ignore remedy grades, and one small card can wrongly exclude the true remedy
cannot be used for more than two rubrics
Holes show only presence or absence, so grading is lost, and any card lacking the remedy eliminates it.
The 'unsafe' (atticoantral) type of chronic suppurative otitis media is dangerous mainly because of:
a central perforation of the pars tensa
Cholesteatoma in the attic erodes bone and leads to intracranial and extracranial complications.
Dysmenorrhoea in which the pains are relieved as soon as the menstrual flow begins is a keynote of:
Lachesis is better once the discharge is established; in Cimicifuga the pain increases as the flow increases.
Kent traced the origin of psora to:
disordered willing and thinking of man, a spiritual sickness that came before the itch
infection by the itch mite alone
Kent (Lectures on Homoeopathic Philosophy) held psora to be the primitive disorder of the human race, arising from man's wrong willing and thinking.
The mature cyst of Entamoeba histolytica contains:
The mature infective cyst of E. histolytica is quadrinucleate; the cyst of the non-pathogenic E. coli has up to eight nuclei.
A baby delivered with the arm pulled upward develops claw hand with Horner's syndrome on that side. The lesion is in the:
lower trunk of the brachial plexus (C8–T1)
upper trunk of the brachial plexus (C5–C6)
This is Klumpke's palsy; T1 involvement interrupts the sympathetic outflow to the head, giving Horner's syndrome.
When a new dissimilar disease has acted on the organism for long and joins the old one, each occupying its own region, Hahnemann (§40) calls the result:
§40: dissimilar diseases may unite into a complex disease, each occupying its own locality in the organism; allopathic drugging commonly produces this.
The standards of the HPI become legally binding because the Drugs and Cosmetics Act names the HPI in its:
The Second Schedule of the Act lists the standards drugs must meet; for homoeopathic medicines it names the HPI (and, failing that, other official homoeopathic pharmacopoeias).
According to §85, while recording the case the physician should:
group the symptoms under the diagnosis
write the symptoms in order of their severity
begin a fresh line with every new symptom, so each stands separately
record only the symptoms that seem important
§85: a fresh line for each new circumstance, symptoms ranged separately one below the other, so each can be completed later.
Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, a drug sold under the name of another drug, or falsely claiming to be made by a certain manufacturer, is termed:
Section 17-B defines spurious drugs (imitations and false claims of identity or maker); 17 covers misbranding and 17-A adulteration.
Under the national programme, the first dose of vitamin A given at 9 months of age is:
The first dose is 1 lakh IU at 9 months with MR; later doses are 2 lakh IU every 6 months up to 5 years.
Rheumatism that begins in the feet and travels upwards is characteristic of:
Ledum: rheumatism begins in the feet and ascends; Kalmia's pains travel downward (Boericke).
Diarrhoea before and during the menses, with the menstrual flow only at night or early morning, is characteristic of:
Bovista (Boericke): diarrhoea before and during menses; flow only at night or early in the morning.
A screening test gives: true positives 80, false negatives 20, false positives 30, true negatives 870. Its sensitivity is:
Sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN) = 80/100 = 80%. 72.7% is the PPV, 96.7% the specificity and 97.8% the NPV.
Called the 'homoeopathic knife' for its power to hasten suppuration in whitlow and abscess, the remedy is:
Myristica sebifera hastens suppuration and is often said to shorten the course of panaritium.
In Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab (2005), the Supreme Court held that to prosecute a doctor for criminal negligence:
any error of judgement is enough
the negligence must be gross or reckless, and a private complaint should be supported by a credible medical opinion
the patient's consent form must be produced first
only a civil suit for compensation is permitted
The judgment set guidelines protecting doctors from frivolous criminal prosecution: simple lack of care is civil; criminal liability needs gross negligence.
In posterior dislocation of the hip, the limb is held in:
Posterior dislocation (dashboard injury) gives flexion, adduction and internal rotation, and may injure the sciatic nerve.
According to §159, the smaller the dose of the homoeopathic remedy:
the smaller and shorter is the homoeopathic aggravation
the longer the remedy must be repeated
the greater the risk of new symptoms
§159: the smaller the dose, the smaller and shorter the apparent increase of the disease in the first hours.
Retention of flatus with distension after abdominal operations, with no passage of gas up or down, calls for:
Raphanus is the noted remedy for postoperative gas retention.
The term 'strangury' in a rubric means:
slow, painful passing of urine drop by drop with straining
passing large amounts of urine at night
Strangury is painful, drop-by-drop urination with tenesmus, as in Cantharis.
The serological marker most specific for rheumatoid arthritis is:
Anti-CCP has a specificity of about 95% for RA; rheumatoid factor is also found in other diseases and in healthy elderly people.
The aphorism that states that in no case is it necessary, and therefore not permissible, to give the patient more than one single simple medicine at a time is:
§273 states the rule of the single remedy (simplex); §§272 to 274 deal with it.
For the LM potency (Organon §270), one grain of the 3C trituration is dissolved in 500 drops of a mixture of:
one part alcohol and four parts water
four parts alcohol and one part water
§270 directs that the grain be dissolved in 500 drops of a mixture of one part alcohol to four parts distilled water.
After a snakebite, blood that fails to clot in the 20-minute whole blood clotting test indicates envenomation by a:
Viper venom is haemotoxic and causes coagulopathy; cobra and krait venoms are neurotoxic.
A patient who feels unusually well the day before an attack of illness, with marked chilliness and offensive discharges, needs:
Psorinum (Allen's Keynotes): feels unusually well the day before an attack.
According to J. H. Allen, the tubercular diathesis (pseudo-psora) is a combination of:
all three miasms in equal parts
J. H. Allen in 'The Chronic Miasms' regarded pseudo-psora (the tubercular diathesis) as a mixed miasm of psora and syphilis.
In case taking (§84), while the patient narrates his sufferings the physician should:
guide the narration with questions from the start
note only the symptoms that fit the diagnosis
ask the relatives first and then the patient
keep silent and not interrupt, noting everything in the patient's own words
§84: the physician lets the patient and friends say all they have to say without interruption and writes it down in their very expressions.
According to §201, in chronic disease the vital force develops a local malady on an external part in order to:
draw attention to the internal organ affected
quiet or silence the internal disease
§201: the vital force produces and keeps up a local symptom on a part not vital to life, to silence the internal disease; removing it externally is harmful.
Fear that she will lose her reason, or that people will notice her confusion, is characteristic of:
Calcarea carb: apprehension, fears losing her reason or that people will observe her confusion (Boericke).
Antimonium tartaricum is tartar emetic, the double tartrate of antimony and potassium; Antimonium crudum is the black sulphide.
A suicidal impulse on seeing a knife or blood is characteristic of:
Alumina (Boericke): suicidal tendency when seeing a knife or blood.
A 3C potency corresponds in degree of dilution to:
Each centesimal step equals two decimal steps (1:100 = 1:10 × 1:10), so 3C = 6X.
Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, the label of a homoeopathic medicine must bear the words:
Rule 106-A requires the words 'Homoeopathic Medicine' on the label, along with the name, potency and other details.
A censorious patient criticises and finds fault with others.
A raised reticulocyte count is most typical of:
Reticulocytosis reflects increased marrow output in response to red cell destruction or blood loss; it is low in marrow failure and deficiency states.
Diabetes following grief, with apathy, indifference, weakness and profuse, milky urine at night, calls for:
Phosphoric acid suits debility from grief with mental apathy and profuse, frequent, milky urine.
Which antihypertensive is contraindicated in pregnancy because of fetal renal damage and oligohydramnios?
ACE inhibitors are fetotoxic; labetalol, methyldopa and nifedipine are the accepted antihypertensives in pregnancy.
For an infant under one month of age, the dose of BCG vaccine is:
BCG is given intradermally in the left upper arm: 0.05 mL up to one month of age and 0.1 mL after that.
The commonest bone fractured during birth is the:
Clavicle fracture is the most frequent birth fracture, often in shoulder dystocia.
drying of tissues in hot, dry air
hydrolysis and hydrogenation of body fat in warm, moist conditions
freezing of body water in cold climates
Adipocere (saponification) is the conversion of fat into a soapy waxy substance in warm, moist surroundings; drying in hot air causes mummification.
According to §71, the three points necessary for cure are knowledge of:
the cause, the pathology and the prognosis of disease
the disease, the powers of medicines, and how to apply them
the miasm, the temperament and the diathesis
the diet, the regimen and the environment
§71: the physician must learn what is to be cured in disease, the pathogenetic powers of medicines, and the mode of employing them.
Pulsatilla nigricans is commonly known as:
Pulsatilla nigricans (Ranunculaceae) is the wind flower or pasque flower; marsh tea is Ledum.
Mental symptoms with a suicidal impulse following an injury to the head, in a patient worse in damp weather, call for:
Natrum sulph: chronic effects of head injuries, mental troubles and suicidal tendency, aggravated by damp (Boericke).
A patient says, 'Nobody cares for me; I am all alone in this world.' The best rubric is:
The feeling of being isolated and uncared for is rubric-converted to 'Forsaken feeling'.
Most of the carbon dioxide in blood is carried as:
About 70% of CO₂ is carried as bicarbonate formed by carbonic anhydrase in red cells.
The clearance of para-aminohippuric acid (PAH) is used to measure:
PAH is filtered and secreted so completely that its clearance approximates renal plasma flow.
In the Weil-Felix test, agglutination of the Proteus OX-K strain alone suggests:
Orientia tsutsugamushi gives OX-K agglutination; epidemic and endemic typhus react with OX-19, and Q fever is Weil-Felix negative.
A chronic, itchy eczema of the antecubital and popliteal fossae in a young adult with a personal history of asthma and hay fever is most likely:
Atopic eczema affects the flexures in older children and adults and is associated with asthma and allergic rhinitis; psoriasis favours extensor surfaces.
Urticaria with burning, itching blotches following the eating of shellfish calls for:
Urtica urens has burning, stinging urticaria and is noted for ailments from eating shellfish.
Red (carneous) degeneration of a fibroid most often occurs:
during pregnancy, usually in the second trimester
in the first year after menarche
during lactation after the sixth month
Red degeneration is a haemorrhagic infarction typically seen in mid-pregnancy, causing acute pain and fever.
moist and pink with intact sensation
Full-thickness burns destroy the nerve endings, so the area is insensate, white or charred and leathery.
The commonest bacterial cause of acute otitis media is:
S. pneumoniae, then H. influenzae and Moraxella, cause most AOM; Pseudomonas and Proteus are typical of CSOM.
A blue line along the gum margins (Burtonian line) is a sign of chronic poisoning by:
The Burtonian line is lead sulphide deposited at the gum margin in chronic lead poisoning.
Rheumatism of the right shoulder (deltoid), so that the arm cannot be raised, is characteristic of:
Sanguinaria: rheumatism of the right shoulder and deltoid, cannot raise the arm (Boericke).
a translation of Boenninghausen's Therapeutic Pocket Book
a repertory of general symptoms only, in three volumes
a card repertory for mechanical elimination
an enlarged and corrected Kent's Repertory, with additions from many sources and author references
Synthesis builds on Kent's 6th edition with corrections, additions and source references; the three-volume generals-only work is Barthel and Klunker's Synthetic Repertory.
In Kent's Repertory, the time sub-rubrics are listed in the order:
morning, forenoon, noon, afternoon, evening, night, midnight
evening, night, midnight, morning, forenoon, noon, afternoon
night, midnight, morning, forenoon, noon, afternoon, evening
Kent lists time through the day starting from morning and ending with night and midnight (and after midnight).
Cerebrospinal fluid is mainly produced by the:
The choroid plexuses secrete CSF; arachnoid granulations absorb it into the venous sinuses.
Hepatitis D virus can cause infection only in the presence of:
HDV is a defective RNA virus that needs HBsAg for its envelope, so it occurs only as co-infection or superinfection with HBV.
Subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord is caused by deficiency of:
B12 deficiency damages the dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts, causing loss of joint position and vibration sense with spastic weakness.
A baby normally begins to smile socially (in response to a face) at about:
The social smile appears at 6–8 weeks; it is a key early social milestone.
Meigs' syndrome is ascites and right-sided hydrothorax associated with:
a granulosa cell tumour of the uterus
Classic Meigs' syndrome is a benign ovarian fibroma with ascites and pleural effusion that resolve after removal.
The secondary attack rate is mainly a measure of:
the case fatality of a disease
the infectiousness (communicability) of a disease among susceptible contacts
the virulence of the agent in the index case
the total burden of disease in the community
Secondary attack rate = cases among contacts within one incubation period / susceptible contacts; Park uses it to measure communicability.
A slight aggravation in the first hours after a well-chosen remedy in an acute disease is, according to §§157 and 158:
a good sign that the disease will probably yield to the first dose
a sign that the remedy was wrong and must be antidoted
a sign that the dose should be repeated at once
a sign that the case is incurable
§158: the slight homoeopathic aggravation in the first hours is a very good prognostic that the acute disease will yield to the first dose.
According to §215, almost all so-called mental and emotional diseases are:
bodily diseases in which the mental symptoms have increased while the bodily symptoms have declined
purely spiritual diseases that need no medicine
diseases caused only by emotional shocks
local diseases of the brain substance
§215: mental diseases are corporeal diseases in which the derangement of mind and disposition has become predominant, like a one-sided disease.
Eruptions behind the ears and in the bends of the joints that ooze a thick, sticky, honey-like fluid, in an obese, chilly, constipated woman, call for:
Graphites: eruptions oozing a thick, honey-like, glutinous fluid, especially behind the ears and in flexures (Allen's Keynotes).
Pyrogenium was made by Drysdale from lean beef left to decompose in the sun; it is used in septic fevers.
A haughty woman to whom objects around her look small, while she feels physically large, needs:
Platina: things look smaller than they are while she feels tall and superior (Boericke).
The size number of a globule (for example No. 10 or No. 30) indicates:
the weight in milligrams of 10 globules
the number of globules in one gram
the number of globules medicated by one drop
the length in millimetres of 10 globules placed in a row
Globule number is the length in mm of ten globules laid side by side, so a No. 10 globule is about 1 mm across.
Causticum (Hahnemann's 'tinctura acris sine kali') is prepared by:
heating oyster shell with flowers of sulphur
distilling freshly slaked lime with a solution of potassium bisulphate
Causticum is the distillate obtained from freshly burnt, slaked lime and a solution of bisulphate of potash.
Loquacity is talkativeness, as in Lachesis.
The ankle jerk tests the spinal segments:
The Achilles reflex is S1–S2; the knee jerk is L3–L4 and the biceps jerk C5–C6.
A blood urea nitrogen (BUN) to creatinine ratio above 20:1 most suggests:
In prerenal states urea is reabsorbed avidly along with water, raising BUN out of proportion to creatinine; in intrinsic renal damage the ratio is usually below 15.
Fever, sore throat, a strawberry tongue, a fine 'sandpaper' rash with circumoral pallor and Pastia's lines suggest:
Scarlet fever, due to erythrogenic toxin of Group A streptococcus, gives this rash with accentuation in skin folds (Pastia's lines).
A first-line oral antiviral for chronic hepatitis B is:
Tenofovir and entecavir are potent nucleos(t)ide analogues with a high barrier to resistance used for chronic HBV.
The commonest cause of fever in the first 24–48 hours after an abdominal operation is:
Early postoperative fever is usually pulmonary collapse; wound infection appears around days 5–7.
Which of the following is NOT one of India's 'Big Four' venomous snakes?
The Big Four are the spectacled cobra, common krait, Russell's viper and saw-scaled viper.
Sharing of fees between a referring doctor and a consultant without the patient's knowledge is called:
Fee-splitting (dichotomy) is infamous conduct; covering is shielding an unqualified person.
In a common-source, single-exposure (point-source) epidemic, the epidemic curve typically shows:
several waves separated by one serial interval each
a slow rise lasting many incubation periods
a steady level of cases over years
a sharp rise and fall, with all cases occurring within one incubation period
A point-source outbreak (e.g. food poisoning) clusters within one incubation period with no secondary waves; propagated epidemics show gradual rise and successive waves.
Carbo vegetabilis is wood (vegetable) charcoal; Carbo animalis is animal charcoal, Spongia roasted sponge and Calcarea carb the middle layer of the oyster shell.
The manner of labelling homoeopathic medicines is laid down specifically in Rule:
Rule 106-A governs the labelling of homoeopathic medicines; Rules 96 and 97 deal with labelling of other drugs and Rule 65 with conditions of retail licences.
The word 'repertory' comes from the Latin 'repertorium', meaning:
a storehouse, a place where things can be found
A repertorium is a storehouse or inventory, an index from which symptoms and remedies can be retrieved.
Fracture of the surgical neck of the humerus endangers the:
The axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck with the posterior circumflex humeral vessels.
Tall, peaked T waves on the ECG are characteristic of:
Raised potassium speeds repolarisation and produces tall tented T waves; hypokalaemia gives flat T waves and U waves.
Kerley B lines on a chest X-ray indicate:
Kerley B lines are short horizontal lines at the lung bases from fluid-thickened interlobular septa, as in left ventricular failure.
Fever with rigors, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain (Charcot's triad) indicate:
Charcot's triad reflects infection of an obstructed common bile duct; adding confusion and hypotension gives Reynolds' pentad.
Urticaria is termed chronic when wheals recur for more than:
Urticaria lasting more than 6 weeks is chronic; second-generation H1 antihistamines are the first-line drugs.
Under the Rome IV criteria, IBS requires recurrent abdominal pain on average at least:
3 days per month in the last 3 months
1 day per week in the last 3 months
Once a month for a year
Rome IV: pain at least 1 day a week for 3 months, with symptom onset at least 6 months before, linked to defecation or change in stool frequency or form; '3 days per month' was Rome III.
Carcinoma of the cervix is most strongly associated with infection by:
High-risk HPV 16 and 18 cause about 70% of cervical cancers.
The ethical principle expressed as 'primum non nocere' is:
Primum non nocere ('first, do no harm') is the principle of non-maleficence.
The Nalgonda technique is used for:
removal of excess fluoride from drinking water
Developed by NEERI, the Nalgonda technique uses alum and lime to defluoridate water; fluoride above 1.5 mg/L causes fluorosis.
Hahnemann's chief remedy for syphilis was:
In 'The Chronic Diseases' Hahnemann treated syphilis with Mercurius; Thuja and Nitric acid were his remedies for sycosis and Sulphur for psora.
Glonoinum is the homoeopathic preparation of:
Glonoinum is nitroglycerine, proved by Hering; silver nitrate is Argentum nitricum.
Which remedy is the chronic complement of Bryonia?
Boericke gives Alumina (and Rhus tox) as complementary to Bryonia; Alumina is called its chronic.
The letter 'D' before a potency number, as used in Germany and Europe, indicates the:
D (decimal) is the European equivalent of X; 6D is the same as 6X.
The patient's statement 'I am always chilly' is classed as a:
It describes the whole person's reaction to temperature, so it is a physical general.
Total body water in an average adult man is about what share of body weight?
About 60% of body weight is water: two-thirds intracellular (40%) and one-third extracellular (20%).
On a chest X-ray, a homogeneous lobar opacity containing air bronchograms most suggests:
Collapse due to an obstructing tumour
Air bronchograms show air-filled bronchi within alveoli filled with exudate, the sign of consolidation; effusion and obstructive collapse do not show them.
A person who has been vaccinated against hepatitis B but never infected will show in serum:
The vaccine contains only HBsAg, so it induces anti-HBs alone; anti-HBc appears only after natural infection.
Pitting of the nails with onycholysis is most characteristic of:
Nail pitting, onycholysis and 'oil-drop' discolouration occur in psoriasis; iron deficiency gives koilonychia.
Conjunctivitis with profuse, acrid, burning tears but a bland nasal discharge calls for:
Euphrasia has acrid lachrymation with bland coryza, the reverse of Allium cepa.
A painless ulcer over the heel or the head of the first metatarsal in a patient with diabetic or leprotic neuropathy is a:
Loss of sensation over pressure points leads to painless perforating trophic ulcers.
According to Nysten's rule, rigor mortis passes off:
in the reverse order of its appearance
all over the body at the same time
in the same order in which it appeared
Rigor appears in eyelids, face, neck, trunk, upper then lower limbs, and passes off in the same sequence.
Which of the following is NOT one of the autonomous boards constituted under the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020?
Medical Assessment and Rating Board for Homoeopathy
Board of Ethics and Registration for Homoeopathy
The NCH Act sets up three autonomous boards: Education, Medical Assessment and Rating, and Ethics and Registration; pharmacopoeia work lies outside it.
According to §99, investigating the case is generally easier in acute than in chronic disease because:
acute diseases have fewer symptoms in every case
acute diseases do not need individualisation
all the phenomena are recent and still fresh in the patient's memory
§99: in acute disease the symptoms are recent and striking, so the investigation is easier and quicker.
the sensation felt by the patient
the pathological diagnosis of the disease
a condition that makes a symptom better or worse
A modality is any circumstance (time, temperature, motion, position, food, weather) that ameliorates or aggravates a symptom.
'The Encyclopedia of Pure Materia Medica' in ten volumes was compiled by:
Timothy Field Allen compiled the 10-volume Encyclopedia of Pure Materia Medica (1874–1879), a schematic pure Materia Medica.
Large, knotty stools held together by threads of mucus are characteristic of:
Graphites: constipation with large, difficult, knotty stools united by mucous threads (Allen's Keynotes).
In chronic typhoid carriers the bacilli most often persist in the:
Chronic carriers harbour Salmonella Typhi in the gall bladder (often with gallstones) and excrete it in faeces.
Bronchitis in an old person with coarse rattling of mucus but very little expectoration, drowsiness and a thick white-coated tongue calls for:
Ant tart has loud rattling with little expectoration, drowsiness and prostration, typical in the very young and the very old.
Eczema with thick, leathery crusts under which thick white pus collects, with intolerable itching, calls for:
Mezereum has eruptions covered by thick, hard crusts with pus beneath, intensely itchy, especially on the scalp.
Under Anemia Mukt Bharat, a pregnant woman takes one IFA tablet (60 mg iron + 500 mcg folic acid) daily from the second trimester for at least:
Prophylactic IFA is given daily from the 4th month of pregnancy for a minimum of 180 days, and continued for 180 days post partum.
A 'thumb sign' on a lateral neck X-ray of a toxic, drooling child is diagnostic of:
The swollen epiglottis appears as a thumb; croup shows a steeple sign on an AP view.
The basic treatment of an established abscess is:
'Where there is pus, let it out': pus must be drained; antibiotics alone do not penetrate an abscess cavity.
A firearm entry wound is characterised by:
everted margins without an abrasion collar
a wound larger than the exit wound in all cases
inverted margins with an abrasion collar
Entry wounds are small with inverted edges and an abrasion (contusion) collar; exit wounds are usually larger and everted, without a collar.
The denominator of the perinatal mortality rate is:
live births plus still births in the year
Perinatal mortality rate = (still births of 28 weeks or more + deaths in the first 7 days) per 1,000 live births plus still births.
According to §27, the curative power of medicines depends on their symptoms being:
opposite to the disease and equal in strength
similar to the disease but weaker than it
identical to the disease in every respect
similar to the disease but stronger than it
§27: the curative power of medicines depends on symptoms similar to the disease but superior to it in strength.
A sense of insecurity in the rectum, with stool escaping when passing flatus and lumps of jelly-like mucus, is characteristic of:
Aloe: insecurity of the rectum, stool passes with flatus, jelly-like mucous lumps (Allen's Keynotes, Boericke).
Which of the following is NOT a nosode?
Pepsinum comes from the healthy stomach of an animal, so it is a sarcode; the others come from disease products.

directions to the patient on how to take it
directions to the pharmacist on how to prepare or dispense the medicine
the name and potency of the medicine
The subscription instructs the dispenser; directions to the patient form the signatura.
Repertories such as Kent's, the TPB and BBCR, in which symptoms are reshaped to fit a fixed plan, belong to the:
These repertories follow a logical plan built on a philosophy, unlike the Puritan works that keep the provers' words.
The normal glomerular filtration rate in an adult is about:
GFR is about 125 mL/min (180 L/day); 650 mL/min is about the renal plasma flow and 1.2 L/min the renal blood flow.
Low serum albumin with a prolonged prothrombin time not corrected by vitamin K indicates:
Impaired synthetic function of the liver
Albumin and clotting factors are made by hepatocytes; failure of both, unresponsive to vitamin K, indicates loss of liver cell mass, as in cirrhosis.
In liver function tests, an AST:ALT ratio greater than 2 suggests:
Alcohol causes pyridoxal phosphate deficiency and mitochondrial damage, so AST rises more than ALT; viral hepatitis usually shows ALT above AST.
Which of the following is used to treat an acute attack of gout?
NSAIDs such as indomethacin, colchicine or corticosteroids treat the acute attack; allopurinol, febuxostat and probenecid are urate-lowering drugs for long-term control.
The antiepileptic drug most strongly associated with neural tube defects when used in pregnancy is:
Valproate carries the highest teratogenic risk, including spina bifida, and is avoided in women of childbearing potential where possible.
Under the UIP, pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV) is given as:
three primary doses at 6, 10 and 14 weeks with no booster
one dose at birth and a booster at 9 months
one dose at 9 months and a booster at 16–24 months
two primary doses at 6 and 14 weeks and a booster at 9 months
India uses a 2+1 PCV schedule: 6 weeks, 14 weeks and a booster at 9–12 months.
The normal range of intraocular pressure is about:
Normal IOP is 10–21 mm Hg; persistent values above this raise suspicion of glaucoma.
Curling's ulcer is an acute stress ulcer of the stomach or duodenum seen after:
Curling's ulcer follows major burns; Cushing's ulcer follows head injury or raised intracranial pressure.
According to the Organon, the complete symptom picture of a prevailing epidemic disease (for the genus epidemicus) is obtained by:
studying the first patient only, as he shows the purest symptoms
consulting the remedy used in the previous epidemic of the same name
noting only the pathological diagnosis common to all patients
careful observation of several cases, since each patient shows only part of the whole picture
Organon §§100-102: each epidemic is treated as new, and the totality is gathered from several cases, as one patient presents only a portion of it.
According to §127, medicines should be proved on:
males only, to avoid confusion with menstrual symptoms
children, as they are most sensitive
the sick, as they react more clearly
§127: medicines must be tested on both sexes, also to reveal the changes they produce in the sexual sphere.
The Arndt-Schulz law, quoted in support of the minimum dose, states that:
the effect of a drug is directly proportional to its dose
weak stimuli excite vital activity, moderate ones favour it, strong ones retard it and very strong ones arrest it
every drug has only one action at all doses
the smaller the dose the stronger the toxic effect
The Arndt-Schulz law describes the opposite actions of small and large stimuli, used to explain the minimum dose.
According to §279, the dose of the correctly chosen homoeopathic remedy:
must be large enough to produce an aggravation
must be increased daily until improvement begins
can never be made so small that it is not stronger than the natural disease
is unimportant if the remedy is similar
§279: the dose of the homoeopathic remedy can never be prepared so small that it is not stronger than the natural disease it can cure.
Digitalis purpurea is prepared from the plant commonly called:
Digitalis is foxglove; monkshood is Aconite, henbane Hyoscyamus and meadow saffron Colchicum.
Boericke: Ammonium carbonicum is inimical to Lachesis.
When Hahnemann's 3C trituration is dissolved in water and alcohol, the first liquid potency obtained is the:
Dissolving the 3C in water and alcohol is itself a further 1:100 step, so the first liquid potency is the 4C (equivalent to 8X).
In Kent's Repertory, a remedy printed in italics carries a value of:
Kent has three grades: bold type 3, italics 2 and plain roman 1.
Mania-a-potu is mania from drink, that is, alcoholic delirium.
Generalised oedema in nephrotic syndrome is mainly due to:
loss of red cells into the tissues
a fall in capillary hydrostatic pressure
a fall in plasma colloid osmotic pressure
Heavy proteinuria lowers plasma albumin, so oncotic pressure falls and fluid leaves the capillaries.
If GFR is 125 mL/min and renal plasma flow is 625 mL/min, the filtration fraction is:
Filtration fraction = GFR ÷ RPF = 125 ÷ 625 = 0.2, that is 20%.
Spread by seeding of body cavities, producing multiple peritoneal deposits, is most characteristic of carcinoma of the:
Transcoelomic seeding of the peritoneal cavity is classically seen with ovarian carcinoma.
Hahnemann recommended which remedy as a prophylactic in epidemics of smooth (Sydenham's) scarlet fever?
In 1801 Hahnemann described Belladonna as the prophylactic for the smooth, bright-red type of scarlet fever, an early use of the genus epidemicus idea.
The commonest cause of acute bronchiolitis in infants is:
RSV causes the majority of bronchiolitis in children under two.
In visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) screening for cervical cancer, the cervix is painted with:
Abnormal epithelium turns acetowhite with 3–5% acetic acid; Lugol's iodine is used for VILI.
Samuel Hahnemann was born in 1755 at:
Hahnemann was born on 10 April 1755 at Meissen, Saxony; he graduated MD from Erlangen in 1779 and later lived at Leipzig and Köthen.
In Kent's first observation, a prolonged aggravation followed by a final decline of the patient means:
the remedy was correct and cure will follow
the remedy was only a palliative
the patient was incurable and the remedy acted too deeply on a weakened vitality
the patient is oversensitive and proves every remedy
Kent (Lectures on Homoeopathic Philosophy): prolonged aggravation with decline shows an incurable patient; the deep antipsoric set up destructive changes.
A sore throat that is better from swallowing solid food, a typical paradoxical symptom, is characteristic of:
Ignatia, the remedy of contradictions: sore throat relieved by swallowing solids (Boericke, Allen).
Plants for homoeopathic drugs should preferably be collected:
from their natural (wild) habitat, in dry and clear weather
at any time and place, as habitat does not matter
from cultivated gardens just after rain
in wet weather when the plant is full of sap
Wild plants from their natural habitat, gathered in dry weather, give the most typical and stable drug.
The symbol 'Rx' at the head of a prescription comes from the Latin 'recipe', meaning:
Rx abbreviates recipe, 'take', the instruction to the dispenser to take the listed ingredients.
A concomitant symptom is best defined as:
a symptom left over from a past illness
a symptom occurring along with the chief complaint without an obvious pathological link to it
the factor that makes the complaint better or worse
A concomitant accompanies the chief complaint in time but is not explained by its pathology; the modifying factor is a modality.
Salivary amylase (ptyalin) begins the digestion of:
Ptyalin splits starch into maltose and dextrins in the mouth.
In hemisection of the spinal cord (Brown-Séquard syndrome), pain and temperature sensation are lost:
on both sides below the lesion
on the opposite side, beginning a segment or two below the lesion
on the same side below the lesion
only at the level of the lesion on the opposite side
Spinothalamic fibres cross within one or two segments, so pain and temperature are lost contralaterally; dorsal-column sensation and motor power are lost on the same side.
The histological grading of a malignant tumour is based mainly on its:
Degree of differentiation and mitotic activity
Grade reflects how closely tumour cells resemble normal cells (differentiation) and mitotic count; size, nodes and metastases determine the stage.
Which of these is a WHO warning sign in dengue that calls for close monitoring or admission?
Warning signs include abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, fluid accumulation, mucosal bleeding, lethargy, liver enlargement and rising haematocrit with falling platelets.
A child can copy a circle at about:
Copying a circle is a 3-year fine motor skill; a triangle is copied at about 5 years.
The first-aid management of an acute ankle sprain is summed up as:
rest and hot fomentation for a week
RICE reduces bleeding and swelling in the first 48–72 hours.
The first aid for an animal bite with suspected rabies exposure is to:
suture the wound tightly at once
wash the wound with soap and running water for about 15 minutes
cover it with a tight bandage without washing
Thorough washing removes much of the virus; the wound is not sutured early, and vaccine with or without RIG follows.
Deep bruising of soft tissues such as the breasts, pelvic organs or abdominal wall after injury or surgery calls for:
Bellis perennis acts on deep tissue trauma, especially of the trunk, breasts and pelvic organs.
